entry.title: skopeo failed to access local registry with error "certificate signed by unknown authority"
entry.content: skopeo is a command line utility that performs various operations on container images and image repositories.Environment macOS Big Sur 11.3.1Issue Failed to run skopeo commands to the local registry, with error “certificate signed by unknown authority”.Resolution Obtain the local registry certificate firstly $ echo -n | openssl s_client -showcerts -connect <local_registry_IP>:443 2>/dev/null | sed -ne '/-BEGIN CERTIFICATE-/,/-END CERTIFICATE-/p' > cert.crt Add the certificate to the Mac’s keychain $ sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain cert.crt Diagnostic Steps At the beginning, I just want to inspect one docker image on the local registry, but found errors as below: $ skopeo inspect --raw docker://9.110.70.75/ibmcom/ibm-storage-odf-operator:0.1.0-73ca917FATA[0000] Error parsing image name "docker://9.110.70.75/ibmcom/ibm-storage-odf-operator:0.1.0-73ca917": error pinging docker registry 9.110.70.75: Get "https://9.110.70.75/v2/": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority Later, I tried to login the same registry but failed with same error. $ skopeo login 9.110.70.75 -u mcdev -p Machinec1tyFATA[0000] error authenticating creds for "9.110.70.75": error pinging docker registry 9.110.70.75: Get "https://9.110.70.75/v2/": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority skopeo does not require a daemon, can’t use configuration file like /etc/docker/daemon.json. So adding the certification to the trusted store should be fine. Referencesskopeo on GitHubAdding Self-signed Registry Certs to Docker & Docker for Mac

entry.title: OCP upgrade stuck by waiting on machine-config
entry.content: I did OCP upgrade several times, found that it often stuck by waiting on machine-config. Not sure the root cause yet, but confirmed a valid workaround.Environment Red Hat OpenShift 4.7Issue OCP upgrade stuck by waiting on machine-config, which reported 99-master-generated-registries controller version mismatch.Resolution Confirm only 99-master-generated-registries controller version old and others already latest. Update its metadata manually by the following command: # oc edit mc 99-master-generated-registriesmetadata: annotations:>> machineconfiguration.openshift.io/generated-by-controller-version: <update_new_version_here> Later the upgrade will continue and finish.Diagnostic Steps Checking current upgrade state, found that only one cluster operator machine-config not available. # date; oc get clusterversionsSat May 8 18:00:47 CST 2021NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING SINCE STATUSversion 4.7.8 True True 7h38m Working towards 4.7.9: 560 of 668 done (83% complete)# date; oc get clusteroperatorsSat May 8 18:01:43 CST 2021NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE...output omitted...machine-config 4.7.8 False True True 6h44m Checking its conditions status, there were two errors which pointed to the controller version mismatch. # date; oc describe clusteroperators machine-configSat May 8 18:08:04 CST 2021Name: machine-configNamespace:Labels: <none>Annotations: exclude.release.openshift.io/internal-openshift-hosted: true include.release.openshift.io/self-managed-high-availability: true include.release.openshift.io/single-node-developer: trueAPI Version: config.openshift.io/v1Kind: ClusterOperator...output omitted...Status: Conditions: ...output omitted... Last Transition Time: 2021-05-08T03:50:07Z Message: Unable to apply 4.7.9: timed out waiting for the condition during syncRequiredMachineConfigPools: pool master has not progressed to latest configuration: controller version mismatch for 99-master-generated-registries expected ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a has 116603ff3d7a39c0de52d7d16fe307c8471330a0: all 3 nodes are at latest configuration rendered-master-1c5dcb64c35c3b6fe87f2ba6c76aa602, retrying Reason: RequiredPoolsFailed Status: True Type: Degraded Last Transition Time: 2021-05-08T03:17:26Z Message: Cluster not available for 4.7.9 Status: False Type: Available Extension: Last Sync Error: pool master has not progressed to latest configuration: controller version mismatch for 99-master-generated-registries expected ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a has 116603ff3d7a39c0de52d7d16fe307c8471330a0: all 3 nodes are at latest configuration rendered-master-1c5dcb64c35c3b6fe87f2ba6c76aa602, retrying Master: all 3 nodes are at latest configuration rendered-master-1c5dcb64c35c3b6fe87f2ba6c76aa602 Worker: all 3 nodes are at latest configuration rendered-worker-d99f619a2e383cf571b689fb8a84f8ee Checking all machineconfig, they should be updated in fact. But 99-master-generated-registries still kept the old one. # date; oc get machineconfigpoolSat May 8 18:14:25 CST 2021NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGEmaster rendered-master-1c5dcb64c35c3b6fe87f2ba6c76aa602 True False False 3 3 3 0 45dworker rendered-worker-d99f619a2e383cf571b689fb8a84f8ee True False False 3 3 3 0 45d# date; oc get machineconfigSat May 8 18:16:25 CST 2021NAME GENERATEDBYCONTROLLER IGNITIONVERSION AGE00-master ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a 3.2.0 45d00-worker ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a 3.2.0 45d01-master-container-runtime ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a 3.2.0 45d01-master-kubelet ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a 3.2.0 45d01-worker-container-runtime ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a 3.2.0 45d01-worker-kubelet ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a 3.2.0 45d03-worker-extensions 3.1.0 40d99-ibm-attach 2.2.0 43d99-master-generated-registries 116603ff3d7a39c0de52d7d16fe307c8471330a0 3.2.0 45d99-master-ssh 3.1.0 45d99-openshift-machineconfig-worker-kargs 40d99-worker-generated-containerruntime ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a 3.2.0 40d99-worker-generated-registries 39de2f3d075d84c945f02d209c02c17b24d5dd71 3.2.0 45d99-worker-ssh 3.1.0 45drendered-master-12b5487116baeb36c4394d6f174a082f 116603ff3d7a39c0de52d7d16fe307c8471330a0 3.2.0 9drendered-master-1c5dcb64c35c3b6fe87f2ba6c76aa602 ac79a2ffc6002f086b3fa80003b278b635d2055a 3.2.0 6h52mrendered-master-99353247eb255890ab38b6681a627f5c 116603ff3d7a39c0de52d7d16fe307c8471330a0 3.2.0 12drendered-master-d5dc1e815e7cd6ee200aad853733c935 a29f0d80366f4a6eb72f163cb11249b8b965a22b 3.2.0 17drendered-worker-1b18f382325f3b810824faf66220e0a3 39de2f3d075d84c945f02d209c02c17b24d5dd71 3.2.0 45d...output omitted... So I tried to update the controller version of 99-master-generated-registriesmanually, and it worked.

entry.title: How to modify the description of a specific commit after pushing
entry.content: Sometimes I found that some commit using the wrong description after the commit already pushed to remote repository, we can use command git commit --amend to update the last commit. But if not the last one?Locate the commit you want to updateTo update the description of some specific commit, you need to find it firstly.$ git logRebase the commitIf the specific commit was the last n commit, issuing the following command:$ git rebase -i HEAD~nUpdate the command from pick to edit on the specific commit, then hit Esc and enter :wq to exit git(vim) environment.Example:edit 24dbd75 Minor changes on the 18th articlepick 1a40b2c Added one reference URL on the 19th articlepick c1c55d6 Added the 21th article# Rebase d8b5c20..77b6cee onto d8b5c20 (5 commands)## Commands:# p, pick <commit> = use commit# r, reword <commit> = use commit, but edit the commit message# e, edit <commit> = use commit, but stop for amending# s, squash <commit> = use commit, but meld into previous commit# f, fixup <commit> = like "squash", but discard this commit's log message# x, exec <command> = run command (the rest of the line) using shell# b, break = stop here (continue rebase later with 'git rebase --continue')# d, drop <commit> = remove commit# l, label <label> = label current HEAD with a name# t, reset <label> = reset HEAD to a label# m, merge [-C <commit> | -c <commit>] <label> [# <oneline>]# . create a merge commit using the original merge commit's# . message (or the oneline, if no original merge commit was# . specified). Use -c <commit> to reword the commit message.## These lines can be re-ordered; they are executed from top to bottom.## If you remove a line here THAT COMMIT WILL BE LOST.## However, if you remove everything, the rebase will be aborted.#Amend the description of the specific commitUpdate the new description by issuing the following command:$ git commit --amendOnce you are satisfied with your changes, run:$ git rebase --continuePush the latest update to remote repository$ git push origin master --force For the shared repository, have better to make sure no new commits from others before you force pushing.ReferenceGit 修改已提交的commit注释

entry.title: Next steps after receiving redhat account activated email
entry.content: Due to new project needs, Red Hat help to create few corporate accounts for us. Its partner manager will forward the IT help desk email to the individual once the account activated. What to do next?Prerequisites The email which have the temporary token code The laptop might access IBM network (office or IBM VPN) The temporary token will be active for the next 5 days since the effective startdate.ProceduresAccess Red Hat mail systemRedhat mail system uses Gmail services, so we need to use a proxy(e.g. proxy.emea.ibm.com:80) at first. Browse to Redhat mail system Sign in with the credentials you got, which have the username and temporary token code. Find an email with subject “New Hire Vital Information PLEASE READ”, follow its guideline to set up permanent passwords. The following steps are same, but with the key points I have verified, just for your reference.Configure the Red Hat VPNBecause we don’t use a laptop provided by Red Hat (tag our laptop as Non-CSB Macs, and their IT does not currently support), but we can set up an OpenVPN client following the article KB0009053. Download VPN profiles from here, unzip the archive. Download the latest stable version of Tunnelblick from here, and install it with option “I have configuration files”. Click the Tunnelblick icon on the top menu bar, select “VPN Details…” to view the configuration window, drag “Red Hat Global VPN.ovpn” from the unzipped VPN profiles folder, choose to add the profile for all users. Repeat this step with any regional servers you want to add. Click the Tunnelblick icon on the top menu bar, select a connection to connect the Red Hat VPN. You might try several times if have some errors.Set a permanent Kerberos passwordThis phase can follow the article KB0000072. Connect to the Red Hat VPN firstly Go to RESET YOUR IPA/KERBEROS PASSWORD portal Complete all the fields with your temporary token, then click “Set” button at the bottom right. If success, it will prompt up a message “SUCCESS. Both IdM and Kerberos Passwords have been reset!”Set up a permanent Pin+TokenRed Hat use a two-part code called a PIN and Token to access the Virtual Private Network (VPN), Workday, and most sites with a URL including “corp.redhat.com.” A PIN is a secret password that you set. A Token is a randomized, one-time use code created by a token device. Because this login method requires two parts, it is also known as “two-factor authentication”(a.k.a. 2FA). EMC did the same when I worked there, here we choose soft token due to we can’t apply hard token device so far.This phase can follow the article KB0004383. Install FreeOTP app on your mobile device. iOS follows up KB0004382, Android system can download the latest apk file from F-Droid due to we can’t access Google Play Store. Connect to the Red Hat VPN, go to RED HAT 2FA with your Kerberos password. On the left side of the page, click Create Software Token, ensure the box for “Generate OTP Key on the Server” is checked under “Token data”. Enter your PIN, click Enroll Token button, a new page will display a QR code. Open the FreeOTP app on your mobile device, tap the QR code symbol to scan the displayed QR code using your camera.Access your Red Hat email with new credentials Connect to the Red Hat VPN or IBM VPN with a proxy, browse to Redhat mail system. Enter your Red Hat email address and 2FA PIN+token if prompted, the soft token can be got by tapping the token on the FreeOTP app.ReferencesRed Hat self-service portalRed Hat IT New Hire HubRed Hat Intranet

entry.title: Can't access OCP console after upgrade
entry.content: I did OCP upgrade from v4.7.3 to v4.7.6 last night, but failed to access OCP console this morning.Environment Red Hat OpenShift 4.7 All master and worker nodes configured with KVM VMsIssue Can’t access OCP console UI from web browserResolution Clean some big files on /var, I chose to clean YUM cache data for temporary. # yum clean all After /var have enough free space, then can resume the VMs. # virsh resume <VM_name> Diagnostic Steps Tried to use command oc login but failed. Checked VMs status, found that only all master nodes in paused state. # virsh list Id Name State---------------------------------------------------- 4 master1 paused 6 master2 paused 8 master3 paused 15 buildserver running Tried to resume and reboot the VMs but not working. After realizing that /var saved the VM images, found it was full. # df -h /varFilesystem Size Used Avail Use% Mounted on/dev/mapper/rhel-var 200G 200G 20K 100% /var Checking the Top-10 files size on /var, found that VM images and YUM cache files. # find /var -type f -print0 | xargs -0 du -h | sort -rh | head -n 1080G /var/lib/libvirt/images/master1.qcow276G /var/lib/libvirt/images/master2.qcow230G /var/lib/libvirt/images/master3.qcow23.3G /var/cache/yum/x86_64/7Server/ftp3/gen/other.xml.sqlite3.2G /var/cache/yum/x86_64/7Server/ftp3/gen/other.xml760M /var/cache/yum/x86_64/7Server/ftp3/fd8840af9aa89e94f8e4570aede2165c9b65aabe-other.xml.gz437M /var/cache/yum/x86_64/7Server/ftp3/gen/primary.xml.sqlite365M /var/cache/yum/x86_64/7Server/ftp3/gen/primary.xml244M /var/lib/rpm/Packages119M /var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/ So cleaned YUM cache to release more space. # yum clean all# df -h /varFilesystem Size Used Avail Use% Mounted on/dev/mapper/rhel-var 200G 192G 8.6G 96% /var Referencevirsh command usage from Red Hat documentation

entry.title: MacOS Spotlight Search doesn't show applications
entry.content: My laptop can’t list applications(e.g. calculator or textedit) on the Spotlight Search, it happened after some upgrade.Environment MacOS Big Sur 11.xIssue After launching Spotlight Search (Shortcut: Command + Space bar), enter an application keyword calc, it only shows the definition list, can’t see a such application what I want as normal.Resolution Disable System Integrity Protection (SIP) firstly Restart your computer in Recovery mode Launch Terminal from the Utilities menu Run the command csrutil disable Restart your computer Rebuild the index Turn off Spotlight by issuing command sudo mdutil -a -i off Unload the metadata file that controls Spotlight’s index sudo launchctl unload -w /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.metadata.mds.plist Re-load the metadata file sudo launchctl load -w /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.metadata.mds.plist Turn Spotlight back on by issuing command sudo mdutil -a -i on Enable System Integrity Protection (SIP) again Restart your computer in Recovery mode Launch Terminal from the Utilities menu Run the command csrutil enable Restart your computer ReferencesSpotlight doesn’t show applicationsMac keyboard shortcutsDisabling and Enabling System Integrity Protection

entry.title: Steps to contribute on Open Source projects
entry.content: Many years ago, I would like be a coding guy but not taking actions for any Open Source projects, because of my limited coding experience.Prerequisites Have taken the required annual open source training Fixing a typo or cleaning up some grammar in a comment or documentation does not require a formal request. Others should apply contribution requests in WICKED, refer to here for more information. The existing github accounts, not only public GitHub account, but also GitHub Enterprise account. Have linked your public GitHub ID to your IBM ID using GitHub User Mapper webpage. Setup authentication between your workstation and GitHub, can refer Connecting to GitHub with SSH for more information.ProceduresFork and clone your interesting project Search your interesting repository from GitHub UI, then clicking on Fork button in the upper right-hand corner. Open a terminal and change into the directory where you want to clone the forked repository. Clone the forked repository onto your workstation with the following command(taking openshift-docs repository as example), replacing with your actual GitHub ID. # git clone git@github.com:<user_name>/openshift-docs.git Change into the directory for the local repository you just cloned. # cd openshift-docs Add an upstream pointer back to the OpenShift’s remote repository, in this case openshift-docs. # git remote add upstream git@github.com:openshift/openshift-docs.git Ensure your local repository is in sync with the remote From your local repository, make sure you have the master branch checked out. # git checkout master If you want to change the contents based on another remote branch, create a local branch which track a remote branch. # git checkout --track origin/<branch_name> Fetch the current state of the OpenShift documentation repository # git fetch upstream Incorporate the commits from the remote repository, in this case openshift/openshift-docs, into your local repository. # git rebase upstream/master Push the latest updates to your forked repository so that it is also in sync with the remote # git push origin master Add content or update existing content on local branch Create local working branch where you will make all your updates, or create any new content. # git checkout -b <working_branch> Create content or update existing content as required, ensure following up documentation guidelines if have. Add all of your changes to a pending commit # git add . Commit your changes # git commit -am "Detailed comments about what changes were made; for example, fixed typo" Rebase updates from master into your working branch # git rebase upstream/master If you find any conflicts you must fix those, and repeat previous two steps. Push all changes to your GitHub account # git push origin <working_branch> Submit PR to merge your work Go to your forked GitHub repository on the GitHub website, and you should see your local branch that includes all of your work. Click on Pull Request to submit the PR against the master branch or another remote branch of the forked repository. Confirm your changes have been merged Just repeat the same steps of “Ensure your local repository is in sync with the remote”.Add changes to an existing PR, if requiredIn some cases you might have to make changes to a PR that you have already submitted. Commit whatever updates you have made to the working branch by creating a new commit # git commit -am "Detailed message as noted earlier" Rebase your PR and squash multiple commits into one commit. # git rebase -i HEAD~n Where n is the number of commits to rebase. Rebase new updates from master into your working branch in case already have # git rebase upstream/master If your commits based on another remote branch, issuing the following command: # git rebase upstream/<branch_name> After you have rebased and squashed, push the latest updates to the local working branch to your GitHub account. # git push origin <working_branch> --force Delete the local working branchWhen you have confirmed that all of your changes have been accepted and merged, and you have pulled the latest changes on master and pushed them to your GitHub account, you can delete the local working branch. Delete the local working branch from your workstation # git branch -D <working_branch> Delete the working branch from your GitHub account # git push origin :<working_branch> ReferencesOpen Source@IBM from W3 DeveloperOpen Source Steering Committee from w3PublisherContributing to Open Source from w3Publisher

entry.title: Steps to install IBM Cloud Platform Common Services on an OCP environment
entry.content: IBM Cloud Platform Common Services provide key foundational services, e.g. logging, monitoring, common web UI and so on. Several IBM Cloud Paks will use some of those services.1. Prerequisites1.1 Environment Preparation Refer hardware sizing requirement in knowledge center An existing OCP cluster (Red Hat OpenShift 4.4 or above), I used OCP v4.6.15 for this setup. For a small profile on a Linux x86_64 cluster, common services need at least 6 VPCs and 10 GB memory, minimum number of worker node is 1. For a medium profile on a Linux x86_64 cluster, common services need at least 13 VPCs and 21 GB memory, minimum number of worker node is 3.1.2 Installation Preparation Ensure that your client have logged in to the web console server, otherwise can’t issue oc commands on your client. # oc login Ensure that can access OCP web console, running following command to check its URL. # oc -n openshift-console get routeNAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARDconsole console-openshift-console.apps.s07.mcocp.com console https reencrypt/Redirect None The console URL in this example is https://console-openshift-console.apps.s07.mcocp.com/. Ensure a DEFAULT storage class, which can be used for creating storage for Common Services. # oc get storageclassesNAME PROVISIONER RECLAIMPOLICY VOLUMEBINDINGMODE ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION AGEsc-iscsi-fs9200-dedup block.csi.ibm.com Delete Immediate true 8dsc-iscsi-fs9200-thin (default) block.csi.ibm.com Delete Immediate true 8d Make a StorageClass as default: # kubectl patch storageclass <storageclass_name> -p '{"metadata": {"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"true"}}}' (Optional) For Elasticsearch of logging service, ensure that the vm.max_map_count setting is at least 262144 on all nodes. # sysctl -a | grep vm.max_map_countvm.max_map_count = 262144 If the vm.max_map_count setting is not at least 262144, complete these steps to set the value to 262144: # cat <<EOF> tuned-cs-es.yamlapiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1kind: Tunedmetadata: name: common-services-es namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operatorspec: profile: - data: | [sysctl] vm.max_map_count=262144 name: common-services-es recommend: - priority: 10 profile: common-services-esEOF # oc create -f tuned-cs-es.yaml 2. Installing the IBM Cloud Platform Common Services operator2.1 Create the IBM Cloud Platform Common Services catalog source. Prepare a YAML file opencloud-operators.yaml and create it. # cat <<EOF> opencloud-operators.yaml apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: CatalogSource metadata: name: opencloud-operators namespace: openshift-marketplace spec: displayName: IBMCS Operators publisher: IBM sourceType: grpc image: docker.io/ibmcom/ibm-common-service-catalog:latest updateStrategy: registryPoll: interval: 45m EOF # oc create -f opencloud-operators.yaml Verify that the source container is running: # oc -n openshift-marketplace get pod | grep opencloud-operators opencloud-operators-65ncp 1/1 Running 0 35s 2.2 Install the IBM Cloud Platform Common Services operator From the navigation pane of OCP web console, click Operators > OperatorHub. In the All Items field, enter IBM Cloud Platform Common Services(for v3.6.x) or IBM Cloud Pak foundational services(for v3.7.x). Click the IBM Cloud Platform Common Services or IBM Cloud Pak foundational services tile, then click Install button. Leave all options as default, click Install button.2.3 Setting the hardware profile to small, default is medium. From the navigation pane of OCP web console, click Home > Search. From the Project drop-down list, select ibm-common-services. From the Resources drop-down list, select CommonService. Click the common-service resource, select the YAML tab. Update the spec.size parameter to small. ...spec: size: small 3. Installing common services in your cluster Prepare a YAML file operand-request.yaml for Common UI as example here and create it. Must read the Common service dependencies before creating the YAML file. # cat <<EOF> operand-request.yamlapiVersion: operator.ibm.com/v1alpha1kind: OperandRequestmetadata: name: common-service namespace: ibm-common-servicesspec: requests: - operands: - name: ibm-cert-manager-operator - name: ibm-mongodb-operator - name: ibm-iam-operator bindings: public-oidc-creds: secret: platform-oidc-credentials public-auth-creds: secret: platform-auth-idp-credentials public-auth-cert: secret: platform-auth-secret public-cam-secret: secret: oauth-client-secret public-cam-map: configmap: oauth-client-map public-auth-config: configmap: platform-auth-idp - name: ibm-management-ingress-operator bindings: public: secret: ibmcloud-cluster-ca-cert configmap: ibmcloud-cluster-info - name: ibm-commonui-operator - name: ibm-ingress-nginx-operator - name: ibm-platform-api-operator registry: common-service registryNamespace: ibm-common-servicesEOF # oc apply -f operand-request.yamloperandrequest.operator.ibm.com/common-service created Verifying the installation # oc get pods -n ibm-common-servicesNAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGEauth-idp-79785b8bcc-z8k2d 4/4 Running 0 11mauth-pap-678ddc74cd-sprwr 2/2 Running 0 16hauth-pdp-8c75fb464-2zr5t 2/2 Running 0 10mcert-manager-cainjector-7c5d667b7-d9vsx 1/1 Running 8 16hcert-manager-controller-595cdc44dd-ql25n 1/1 Running 0 16hcert-manager-webhook-798d55f5-8pdhv 1/1 Running 0 16hcommon-web-ui-84db654d9d-q7k55 2/2 Running 4 16hconfigmap-watcher-587667b6dd-55dvz 1/1 Running 0 16hdefault-http-backend-8659c9f69b-fxs77 1/1 Running 0 16hiam-onboarding-2k8mp 0/1 Completed 0 8m7siam-policy-controller-c994c58cf-8g962 1/1 Running 0 16hibm-cert-manager-operator-7ff94cb867-hrt4q 1/1 Running 0 16hibm-common-service-webhook-dbd6778cb-4c4xp 1/1 Running 0 5d20hibm-commonui-operator-69d9fc855-lmpjg 1/1 Running 0 16hibm-iam-operator-68db9bbdd9-nmv8z 1/1 Running 0 16hibm-ingress-nginx-operator-79d9649689-7ztlw 1/1 Running 0 16hibm-management-ingress-operator-76997c6c9c-tkf6z 1/1 Running 0 16hibm-mongodb-operator-8c88ddf4b-fjmd8 1/1 Running 0 16hibm-namespace-scope-operator-5659c8d556-hqrrp 1/1 Running 0 5d20hibm-platform-api-operator-b56b6cd58-x9zzw 1/1 Running 4 16hicp-mongodb-0 2/2 Running 0 7m11smanagement-ingress-7d4c45b444-64xww 1/1 Running 0 16hnginx-ingress-controller-6b49ffdbb5-v7bq6 1/1 Running 0 16hoidc-client-registration-csppq 0/1 Completed 0 16hoidcclient-watcher-6758986b95-mtpqq 1/1 Running 0 7m11soperand-deployment-lifecycle-manager-8687fd5d45-7gm46 1/1 Running 0 5d20hplatform-api-75b4ff5f66-w7xrw 2/2 Running 0 16hsecret-watcher-64b4cf87fc-pk62c 1/1 Running 0 6m2ssecretshare-6b985c4fd7-f22w5 1/1 Running 0 5d20hsecurity-onboarding-69fbj 0/1 Completed 0 5m55s # oc -n ibm-common-services get csvNAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASEibm-cert-manager-operator.v3.8.1 IBM Cert Manager 3.8.1 ibm-cert-manager-operator.v3.8.0 Succeededibm-common-service-operator.v3.6.3 IBM Cloud Platform Common Services 3.6.3 ibm-common-service-operator.v3.6.2 Succeededibm-commonui-operator.v1.4.1 Ibm Common UI 1.4.1 ibm-commonui-operator.v1.4.0 Succeededibm-iam-operator.v3.8.2 IBM IAM Operator 3.8.2 ibm-iam-operator.v3.8.1 Succeededibm-ingress-nginx-operator.v1.4.1 IBM Ingress Nginx Operator 1.4.1 ibm-ingress-nginx-operator.v1.4.0 Succeededibm-management-ingress-operator.v1.4.3 Management Ingress Operator 1.4.3 ibm-management-ingress-operator.v1.4.2 Succeededibm-mongodb-operator.v1.2.1 IBM MongoDB Operator 1.2.1 ibm-mongodb-operator.v1.2.0 Succeededibm-namespace-scope-operator.v1.0.1 IBM NamespaceScope Operator 1.0.1 ibm-namespace-scope-operator.v1.0.0 Succeededibm-platform-api-operator.v3.8.1 IBM Platform API 3.8.1 ibm-platform-api-operator.v3.8.0 Succeededoperand-deployment-lifecycle-manager.v1.4.2 Operand Deployment Lifecycle Manager 1.4.2 operand-deployment-lifecycle-manager.v1.4.1 Succeeded Accessing the console Use the following command to get the console URL # oc get route -n ibm-common-services cp-console -o jsonpath=‘{.spec.host}’ ‘cp-console.apps.s07.mcocp.com’ Based on the above example output, the console URL would be https://cp-console.apps.s07.mcocp.com:443. Add the entry to the /etc/hosts in your laptop 9.115.251.187 mc187 cp-console.apps.s07.mcocp.com Log in to IBM Cloud Pak Administration Hub with above console URL, select authentication type OpenShift authentication, then you can use kubeadmin to login it. 4. Uninstalling common services and the relevant CRDs Refer uninstallation in Knowledge Center Uninstalling all services 1) Uninstall the IBM Cloud Platform Common Services operator From the navigation pane of OCP web console, click Operators > Installed Operators Switch to the project ibm-common-services, locate the IBM Cloud Platform Common Services operator. Select the action Uninstall Operator 2) Delete the operator APIs from the ibm-common-services namespace. Delete the OperandRequest instances Click Operators > Installed Operators > Operand Deployment Lifecycle Manager > OperandRequest Delete all the OperandRequest instances that you created common-serviceibm-iam-requestibm-mongodb-requestmanagement-ingressplatform-api-requestibm-commonui-request Wait for the OperandRequest instances to be deleted Delete the OperandConfig instances Click Operators > Installed Operators > Operand Deployment Lifecycle Manager > OperandConfig Delete all the OperandConfig instances (e.g. common-service here) Delete the OperandRegistry instances Click Operators > Installed Operators > Operand Deployment Lifecycle Manager > OperandRegistry Delete all the OperandRegistry instances (e.g. common-service here) Delete the NamespaceScope instances Click Operators > Installed Operators > IBM NamespaceScope Operator > Namespace Scope Delete all the NamespaceScope instances (e.g. common-service and nss-managedby-odlm here) 3) Uninstall the Operand Deployment Lifecycle Manager operator From the navigation pane of OCP web console, click Operators > Installed Operators Switch to the project ibm-common-services, locate the Operand Deployment Lifecycle Manager operator operator. Select the action Uninstall Operator You also can run the following script to remove all services components, it will do the same actions from above three steps. # bash <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/ibm-common-service-operator/master/common/scripts/force-uninstall.sh) 4) Remove the following configmaps and namespace # oc -n kube-system delete secret icp-mongodb-admin # oc -n kube-system delete secret icp-mongodb-client-cert # oc -n kube-system delete secret icp-serviceid-apikey-secret # oc -n kube-public delete configmap ibm-common-services-status # oc delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration ibm-common-service-webhook-configuration # oc delete namespace services Manually delete the CRDs that you do not want 1) Get the CRDs # oc get crd | grep ibm.com | grep -v csi | grep -v scale authentications.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:25Z certmanagers.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:33Z clients.oidc.security.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:25Z commonservices.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-07T08:37:21Z commonwebuis.operators.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:30Z iampolicies.iam.policies.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:24Z legacyheaders.operators.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:30Z managementingresses.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:36Z mongodbs.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:44Z namespacescopes.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-07T08:38:02Z navconfigurations.foundation.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:31Z nginxingresses.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:41Z oidcclientwatchers.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:24Z operandbindinfos.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-07T08:38:48Z operandconfigs.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-07T08:38:48Z operandregistries.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-07T08:38:48Z operandrequests.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-07T08:38:48Z paps.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:24Z platformapis.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:46Z podpresets.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-07T08:38:12Z policycontrollers.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:25Z policydecisions.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:25Z secretshares.ibmcpcs.ibm.com 2021-02-07T08:38:18Z secretwatchers.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:25Z securityonboardings.operator.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:25Z switcheritems.operators.ibm.com 2021-02-12T12:47:30Z 2) Delete the CRDs that you do not want # oc delete crd <CRD1>, <CRD2>, ..., <CRDn> One-line command for this example ONLY: # for i in `oc get crd | grep ibm.com | grep -v csi | grep -v scale | awk -F " " '{print $1}'`; do oc delete crd $i; done If some crd deletion stuck, empty the finalizers. # oc patch crd <CRDx> -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' --type=merge One-line command for this example ONLY: # for i in `oc get crd | grep ibm.com | grep -v csi | grep -v scale | awk -F " " '{print $1}'`; do oc patch crd $i -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' --type=merge; done Manually delete the namespace ibm-common-services if still there # oc delete ns ibm-common-services 5. ReferencesIBM Cloud Platform Common Services from Knowledge CenterIBM Cloud Pak for Integration from Knowledge CenterBedrock Services from GitHub

entry.title: Steps to install IBM Cloud Pak for Integration on an OCP environment
entry.content: IBM Cloud Pak for Integration(aka CP4I) brings together proven, best-in-class capabilities to deliver a streamlined integration solution. CP4I offers many components, you can install some of them.1. Prerequisites1.1 Environment Preparation An existing OpenShift 4.6.x cluster, I used OCP v4.6.17 for this setup. The OpenShift cluster have defined appropriate storage classes that meet the requirements of the respective integration capability, can refer here for more information. Added the IBM Operator Catalog and the IBM Common Services Catalog to your cluster, can refer here for more information.1.2 Installation Preparation Ensure that your client have logged in to the web console server, otherwise can’t issue oc commands on your client. # oc login Ensure that can access OCP web console, running following command to check its URL. # oc -n openshift-console get routeNAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARDconsole console-openshift-console.apps.s07.mcocp.com console https reencrypt/Redirect None The console URL in this example is https://console-openshift-console.apps.s07.mcocp.com/. To run software from the IBM Entitled Registry, you must supply your entitlement key as a Kubernetes pull secret. 1) Obtain an Entitlement key from IBM Container Library. 2) Adding an entitlement key to a namespace # oc create secret docker-registry ibm-entitlement-key \ --docker-username=cp \ --docker-password=<entitlement-key> \ --docker-server=cp.icr.io \ --namespace=openshift-operators Add the required label to the default namespace # oc label namespace default 'network.openshift.io/policy-group=ingress' 2. Installing the IBM Cloud Pak for Integration operator Search “IBM Cloud Pak for Integration” operator on OperatorHub under all projects, install it. It will install other relevant operators together. From the navigation pane of OCP web console, click Operators > OperatorHub. In the All Items field, enter IBM Cloud Pak for Integration. Click the IBM Cloud Pak for Integration tile, then click Install button. Leave all options as default, click Install button. Deploying Common Service instance if not have From the left navigation pane of OCP web console, click Operators > Installed Operators. Click IBM Cloud Platform Common Services under project ibm-common-services. From the tab Common Service, click the button Create CommonService. Leave all other options as default, click Create button. Updating OpenShift authentication before installing the IAM Operator After Common Service instance created, click the instance common-service to edit. From the YAML tab, scroll down to spec section, add below content and then click Save button. spec: services: - name: ibm-iam-operator spec: authentication: config: preferredLogin: ROKS roksEnabled: true roksURL: 'https://oauth-openshift.apps.s07.mcocp.com' roksUserPrefix: '' 3. Deploying Platform Navigator instance Deployment using the Red Hat OpenShift web console From the left navigation pane of OCP web console, click Operators > Installed Operators. Click IBM Cloud Pak for Integration Platform Navigator under project openshift-operators. From the tab Platform Navigator, click the button Create PlatformNavigator. Change the License Accept option to true. Leave all other options as default, click Create button. This phase might hit the issue#1 and issue#2, check the issues section for more information. Verifying the deployment progress, it will install Common UI too. From the instance, its status should be changed to “Condition: Ready”. # oc get pod -n openshift-operators...integration-navigator-ibm-inte-3c22-deployment-885cfb758-fxr8z 2/2 Running 0 9m43sintegration-navigator-ibm-inte-3c22-deployment-885cfb758-hdrxp 2/2 Running 0 9m44s This phase might hit the issue#3, check the issues section for more information. Accessing the Platform Navigator Use the following command to get the URL # oc get routes -n openshift-operatorsNAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARDintegration-navigator-pn integration-navigator-pn-openshift-operators.apps.s07.mcocp.com integration-navigator-ibm-integration-platform-navigator-ui <all> reencrypt/Redirect None Add the entry to the /etc/hosts in your laptop 9.115.251.187 mc187 integration-navigator-pn-openshift-operators.apps.s07.mcocp.com 4. Installing other common services if needed Prepare a YAML file operand-request.yaml for Common UI and create it # cat <<EOF> operand-request.yamlapiVersion: operator.ibm.com/v1alpha1kind: OperandRequestmetadata: name: common-service namespace: ibm-common-services labels: app.kubernetes.io/instance: operand-deployment-lifecycle-manager app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: operand-deployment-lifecycle-manager app.kubernetes.io/name: odlmspec: requests: - operands: - name: ibm-healthcheck-operator - name: ibm-licensing-operator bindings: public-api-token: secret: ibm-licensing-token public-api-upload: secret: ibm-licensing-upload-token configmap: ibm-licensing-upload-config - name: ibm-metering-operator bindings: public: secret: icp-metering-api-secret - name: ibm-events-operator - name: ibm-elastic-stack-operator bindings: public-certs: secret: logging-elk-certs public-passphrases: secret: logging-elk-elasticsearch-pki-secret - name: ibm-auditlogging-operator bindings: public: secret: audit-server-certs configmap: audit-logging-fluentd-ds-httpingest-url registry: common-service registryNamespace: ibm-common-servicesEOF # oc apply -f operand-request.yamloperandrequest.operator.ibm.com/common-service created 5. Uninstalling the IBM Cloud Pak for Integration5.1 Removing the operands using Openshift web console From the left navigation pane of OCP web console, click Operators > Installed Operators. Select the namespace your operands are deployed, e.g. openshift-operators and ibm-common-services here. Delete the operands associated with the operator using the tabs for each Custom Resource managed by the operator. From Platform Navigators -> integration-navigator instance From the OperandRequest tab of ODLM, delete the OperandRequest common-service. 5.2 Uninstalling the operators using Openshift web console From the left navigation pane of OCP web console, click Operators > Installed Operators. Select the namespace all projects, uninstall below operators one by one. Operator for Apache CouchDBIBM DataPower GatewayIBM API ConnectIBM Aspera HSTSIBM Cert ManagerIBM Operator for RedisIBM Cloud Platform Common ServicesIBM Cloud Pak for IntegrationIBM Event StreamsIBM Cloud Bak for Integration Asset RepositoryIBM Cloud Bak for Integration Operations DashboardIBM Cloud Bak for Integration Platform NavigatorIBM MQIBM NamespaceScope OperatorOperand Deployment Lifecycle Manager 5.3 Removing the remaining deployment and services if have Verify if have remaining deployment on previous deployed namespace # oc get deployments -n openshift-operators# oc get deployments -n ibm-common-services Examples:# oc get deployments -n openshift-operatorsNo resources found in openshift-operators namespace.# oc get deployments -n ibm-common-servicesNAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGEibm-common-service-webhook 1/1 1 1 9dsecretshare 1/1 1 1 9d Delete the remaining deployments # oc delete deployments ibm-common-service-webhook -n ibm-common-servicesdeployment.apps "ibm-common-service-webhook" deleted# oc delete deployments secretshare -n ibm-common-servicesdeployment.apps "secretshare" deleted Verify if have remaining services on previous deployed namespace # oc get services -n openshift-operators# oc get services -n ibm-common-services Examples:# oc get services -n openshift-operatorsNo resources found in openshift-operators namespace.# oc get services -n ibm-common-servicesNAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGEibm-common-service-webhook ClusterIP None <none> 443/TCP 9d Delete the remaining services # oc delete services ibm-common-service-webhook -n ibm-common-servicesservice "ibm-common-service-webhook" deleted 5.4 Remove the following configmaps and namespace Verify the remaining secrets and configmap # oc -n kube-system get secret | grep icp# oc -n kube-public get configmap | grep ibm Example:# oc -n kube-system get secret | grep icpicp-metering-api-secret kubernetes.io/tls 3 12dicp-mongodb-admin Opaque 2 9dicp-mongodb-client-cert kubernetes.io/tls 3 9dicp-serviceid-apikey-secret Opaque 1 9d # oc -n kube-public get configmap | grep ibmibm-common-services-status 1 9d Delete the remaining secrets, configmap and namespace # oc -n kube-system delete secret icp-metering-api-secret# oc -n kube-system delete secret icp-mongodb-admin# oc -n kube-system delete secret icp-mongodb-client-cert# oc -n kube-system delete secret icp-serviceid-apikey-secret# oc -n kube-public delete configmap ibm-common-services-status# oc delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration ibm-common-service-webhook-configuration# oc delete namespace services Verify the remaining namespacescopes # oc -n ibm-common-services get namespacescopes Example:# oc -n ibm-common-services get namespacescopesNAME AGEcommon-service 9dnamespacescope 9dnss-managedby-odlm 9d Delete the remaining namespacescopes # for i in `oc -n ibm-common-services get namespacescopes | grep -v NAME | awk -F " " '{print $1}'`; do oc -n ibm-common-services patch namespacescopes $i -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' --type=merge; done# oc -n ibm-common-services delete namespacescopes common-service# oc -n ibm-common-services delete namespacescopes namespacescope# oc -n ibm-common-services delete namespacescopes nss-managedby-odlm Delete the namespace used for CP4I # oc delete ns ibm-common-services 5.5 Manually delete the relevant CRDs if needed # for i in `oc get crd | grep ibm.com | grep -v csi | grep -v scale | awk -F " " '{print $1}'`; do oc delete crd $i; done6. Issues I metIssue#1Openshift Console showed the operator IBM DataPower Gateway v1.2.0 as failedAfter checking the POD events, it showed below warning, but it is a known issue and fixed by IBM DataPower Gateway v1.2.1. So this version v1.2.0 can be removed directly. Warning FailedScheduling 14s default-scheduler 0/6 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints (missing required label), 3 node(s) had taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master: }, that the pod didn't tolerate.Issue#2Can’t remove IBM DataPower Gateway v1.2.0The operator is a deployment, if deleting it via oc directly, it will be started a new one by OLM.To delete it, list the failed operator under Installed Operators of OpenShift web console, click action Delete ClusterServiceVersion, ensure the checkbox of Delete dependent objects of this resource selected, then click Delete button.Issue#3Many PODs failed to be running during deploying Platform Navigator instance# oc get podNAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGEalertmanager-ibm-monitoring-alertmanager-0 3/3 Running 0 12mauth-pap-77fc94859-q7rvc 2/2 Running 0 16mauth-pap-77fc94859-z4cjf 2/2 Running 0 16mauth-pdp-546f564479-hd7rb 1/2 CreateContainerConfigError 0 16mauth-pdp-546f564479-v8wpd 1/2 CreateContainerConfigError 0 16mauth-pdp-5f49dccdb9-4b96c 1/2 CreateContainerConfigError 0 14mcert-manager-cainjector-cf66985fb-pzcv9 1/1 Running 0 45mcert-manager-controller-69bf69d79b-chb8k 1/1 Running 0 45mcert-manager-webhook-798d55f5-mzd8j 1/1 Running 2 45mcommon-web-ui-8588fc7876-x5t5z 1/2 CreateContainerConfigError 0 16mcommon-web-ui-8588fc7876-xt662 1/2 CreateContainerConfigError 0 16mconfigmap-watcher-87776db9f-5vkx7 1/1 Running 0 45mdefault-http-backend-75c8b889cb-szhqv 1/1 Running 0 14miam-onboarding-7rnkd 0/1 Init:0/5 0 16miam-policy-controller-55645f9d88-nlgq5 1/1 Running 0 16mibm-cert-manager-operator-7ff94cb867-k8md9 1/1 Running 0 45mibm-common-service-webhook-dbd6778cb-gwmxr 1/1 Running 0 47mibm-commonui-operator-69d9fc855-wjpn8 1/1 Running 0 17mibm-iam-operator-68db9bbdd9-k4gqf 1/1 Running 0 17mibm-ingress-nginx-operator-79d9649689-kszv5 1/1 Running 0 15mibm-management-ingress-operator-76997c6c9c-rgvsb 1/1 Running 0 15mibm-mongodb-operator-8c88ddf4b-zdld8 1/1 Running 0 15mibm-monitoring-collectd-7cfd6866b7-xqjlg 2/2 Running 0 16mibm-monitoring-exporters-operator-7577f49fc8-5zns8 1/1 Running 0 17mibm-monitoring-grafana-9b759c6fc-j4595 2/3 Running 7 16mibm-monitoring-grafana-operator-7468d6c9bc-s7ghm 1/1 Running 0 17mibm-monitoring-kube-state-68d7d87bf-pm9v8 2/2 Running 0 16mibm-monitoring-mcm-ctl-5454c586cc-xhjjg 1/1 Running 0 13mibm-monitoring-nodeexporter-2698h 2/2 Running 0 16mibm-monitoring-nodeexporter-bbmx2 2/2 Running 0 16mibm-monitoring-nodeexporter-fbw65 2/2 Running 0 16mibm-monitoring-prometheus-operator-65b5b97f99-6jz5b 1/1 Running 0 13mibm-monitoring-prometheus-operator-ext-6f4bf48dcd-n8xlr 1/1 Running 1 17mibm-namespace-scope-operator-5659c8d556-xgm88 1/1 Running 0 47mibm-platform-api-operator-b56b6cd58-7cg2g 1/1 Running 0 15micp-mongodb-0 2/2 Running 0 15micp-mongodb-1 2/2 Running 0 13micp-mongodb-2 2/2 Running 0 8m38smanagement-ingress-67558d45cf-5ggnp 0/1 CreateContainerConfigError 0 13mmanagement-ingress-67558d45cf-dxzbs 0/1 CreateContainerConfigError 0 13mnginx-ingress-controller-7bd9f6c97d-6fdls 1/1 Running 1 14mnginx-ingress-controller-7bd9f6c97d-qhrmh 1/1 Running 0 14moidc-client-registration-vxr9q 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16moidcclient-watcher-7bb54c84d-8p6q2 0/1 Init:0/3 0 16moperand-deployment-lifecycle-manager-8687fd5d45-rjzlx 1/1 Running 0 46mplatform-api-65f887b854-564dn 2/2 Running 0 15mprometheus-ibm-monitoring-prometheus-0 3/4 CrashLoopBackOff 7 12msecret-watcher-9759784b7-zmlp6 0/1 CreateContainerConfigError 0 16msecretshare-6b985c4fd7-zvtjc 1/1 Running 0 47msecurity-onboarding-bcc4c 0/1 Init:0/1 0 16mAfter checking POD events, the issue should be caused by some secrets delayed creation. After deleting one POD auth-pdp only then all failing PODs continue to be running.Issue#4During deploying Platform Navigator instance, the secret “integration-navigator-ibm-inte-3c22-oidc-client” was not generatedintegration-navigator-ibm-inte-3c22-deployment-885cfb758-g4t8n 0/2 CreateContainerConfigError 0 157mintegration-navigator-ibm-inte-3c22-deployment-885cfb758-t5wdc 0/2 CreateContainerConfigError 0 157m Warning Failed 134m (x6 over 135m) kubelet Error: secret "integration-navigator-ibm-inte-3c22-oidc-client" not found Normal Pulled 134m (x5 over 135m) kubelet Container image "cp.icr.io/cp/icp4i/icip-services:2020-11-25-1623-b398b7d7@sha256:9c97d5d91105adbfb93f8faddf02c8ac7e26e90b7cf21eb3fb3e9b580db4ac28" already present on machine Warning Failed 8m29s (x584 over 139m) kubelet Error: secret "integration-navigator-ibm-inte-3c22-oidc-client" not found Normal Pulled 3m31s (x606 over 135m) kubelet Container image "cp.icr.io/cp/icp4i/icip-navigator:2020-11-27-1400-bbd1e584@sha256:06f661223964e7074e603462aadf6a74b9d7b1339d7bdf8db86d76ae92c7cb9d" already present on machineAfter further check, it should be caused by the previous uninstallation not clean, because one resource under client was remaining.# oc get Client -n openshift-operatorsNAME AGEintegration-navigator-ibm-inte-3c22-oidc-client 27dRemove it before next new deployment then solve the issue, might empty finalizer too.Issue#5Can’t delete namespace ibm-common-servicesThe namespace ibm-common-services stuck in the phase “Terminating”, if edit the namespace then can see the conditions showing below reason: - lastTransitionTime: "2021-02-26T02:56:41Z" message: 'Some resources are remaining: namespacescopes.operator.ibm.com has 2 resource instances' reason: SomeResourcesRemain status: "True" type: NamespaceContentRemaining - lastTransitionTime: "2021-02-26T02:56:41Z" message: 'Some content in the namespace has finalizers remaining: finalizer.nss.operator.ibm.com in 2 resource instances' reason: SomeFinalizersRemain status: "True" type: NamespaceFinalizersRemaining phase: TerminatingIn this case, we can find two resources still remaining on namespacescopes.# oc get namespacescopes.operator.ibm.comNAME AGEcommon-service 26hnss-managedby-odlm 26hTo remove them, empty the finalizers then the namespace will be gone.# for i in `oc -n ibm-common-services get namespacescopes | grep -v NAME | awk -F " " '{print $1}'`; do oc -n ibm-common-services patch namespacescopes $i -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' --type=merge; done7. entry.title: How to install open source tools for AIX
entry.content: AIX tar failed to extract some compressed file, you need to use GNU tar utility (aka gtar here) refer to this KB.There is an AIX Toolbox for Linux Applications, which contains a collection of open source and GNU software built for AIX IBM Systems.Steps to install AIX Toolbox for Linux Applications Download YUM installation script yum.sh directly, then upload it to your AIX. Issuing below commands to install rpm.rte and all the packages needed for yum # chmod +x yum.sh# ./yum.sh# yum update // Update packages to the latest level Install the required packages via YUM command Issuing the yum command like Linux world # yum install -y tar# gtar --help ReferencesAIX Toolbox for Linux Applications The output of running yum.sh # ./yum.shAttempting download of rpm.rte & yum_bundle.tar ...Installing rpm.rte at the latest version ...This may take several minutes depending on the number of rpms installed...+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+ Pre-installation Verification...+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+Verifying selections...doneVerifying requisites...doneResults...
