entry.title: Steps to run regression tests on a PTF build
entry.content: There are some regression testing on a PTF build, I collected some of them here, which I was doing so far. It is not a full list but limited, just for your reference.Filesystem Core RegressionPrerequisites An existing GPFS cluster with a PTF build, and have one filesystem mounted. The testing filesystem must be created with 4 disks(NSD), due to some script need at least 3 disks in the system pool. And one step will remove one disk for testing in the middle of the testing. Mount it2n01:/u/gpfstest on all testing nodes, ensure the variable PATH added the path /u/gpfstest/bin too. Define a file /nodes with specific nodes name which will be used, and they should have installed python3. If the OS is AIX, ensure a symbolic link /usr/bin/python3 linked to the real python3 executable file.Steps to run the regression test Depend on what kinds of testing what you will run(e.g. gerontion or quota testing), you might add users on all nodes firstly. # /u/gpfstest/config/OS/userAdd --numUser 256 -u 94613 -g 100 -p pfs --fvt This command will run hours in my testing, can do it on a screen session. Run the test command, it will call sub-scripts. Example:# nohup /u/gpfstest/bin/regressiontest --no -F fs1 -x --startstress="/u/gpfstest/bin/gerontion -N /nodes -F fs1 --ea --acl --dio --aio --vio --compress ioMixer cacheFiller aclStress" --stopstress="/u/gpfstest/bin/gerontion_killer ioMixer cacheFiller aclStress" >> ~/regressiontest-fs1-15Jan.log & Above command run testing against file system fs1 and redirect the output to log file regressiontest-fs1-15Jan.log mmbackup and HSM RegressionPrerequisites One existing TSM server and one or two TSM clients (HSM node) An existing GPFS cluster with a PTF build, and have one filesystem mounted. The testing filesystem must enable DMAPI function Mount it2n01:/u/gpfstest on all testing nodes You might need two HSM nodes for some test caseSteps to run the regression test Start DMAPI related service firstly if not yet # dsmmigfs start Enable DMAPI function on the testing filesystem # mmumount <filesystem> -a# mmchfs <filesystem> -z yes // Enable DMAPI function on the specific file system# mmmount <filesystem> -a Examples:# mmumount fs1 -a# mmchfs fs1 -z yes# mmmount fs1 -a Add HSM support for the filesystem firstly # dsmmigfs Add /gpfs/fs1 I hit the error ANS9543W once due to the file system issue, it is ok after re-mounting it. Run mmbackup regression test Example:# /u/gpfstest/regression/backup_archive/TSM/mmbackupreg.pl -f fs1 -N <worker_node> -l /log/mmbackup -m 2 -v 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10 The test case2 will be failed always, so bypass here. Run HSM regression test Example:# /u/gpfstest/regression/backup_archive/TSM/hsmreg.pl -f fs1 -l /log/mmbackup // Run all cases# /u/gpfstest/regression/backup_archive/TSM/hsmreg.pl -f fs1 -l /log/mmbackup -v 8 -t 900 The test case5 need two HSM nodes, and have better to add custom timeout(e.g. -t 900) for the test case8. Multicluster and Ciperlist rotation RegressionPrerequisites Two existing GPFS clusters with a PTF build The client cluster(clusterB) mount a remote GPFS filesystem of server cluster(clusterA), the I/O will be ran on the mounted file system. You can refer to this article to setup a multicluster environment. Have better not to start filesystem core regression test at the same time, because it might shutdown the NSD node if it is also configured for the remote file system in your environment.Steps to run the regression test Run I/O on the mounted remote file system, such as blast or vdbench and so on. Update a different security level on the server cluster(clusterA) during I/Os running, the existing I/O should not be interrupted. # mmauth show ciphers // To find a list of supported ciphers# mmauth update <clusterB> -l AES128-SHA // Assuming previous security level was AUTHONLY # mmauth update <clusterB> -l AES256-SHA256 References The help output of regressiontest # /u/gpfstest/bin/regressiontest -hCommand issued was /u/gpfstest/bin/regressiontest -h Great, GPFS is installed. Continuing.Daemon is at 2305 but cluster is at 2301. Do not run mmchfs -V full Usage: regressiontest -f filesystem [-d firstDisk] [-s secondDisk] [-t thirdDisk|NONE] [-n nodeName] [-M] [-x] [-l numberOfLoops] [-p pauseBetweenCommands] [-m pauseForMount] [--startstress="scriptToStartStress"] [--stopstress="scriptToKillStress"] [--gerontionCommands=commaSeparatedList] [--gerontionFlags="flags"] [-w WinDriveLetter] [--nosnapshots] [--nofilesets] [--norecovery] [--noclones] [--nosobar] [--tokencheck] [--mmcrfs-undoc] [--snc] [--forcediffblocksizes] [--no] [--skipsmallfs] [--runonlysmallfs] [--norestorefs] [--tracescope] [--mmdefragfs] [--longUsage|--help] [--bypassfsckprompt] [--4kdisk] [--express] [--skipquotas] [--time] [--skipnetverify] If -d, -s or -t are not specified random disks in the file system will be chosen at the beginning of each loop.If -t NONE is specified then a third disk will not be used (old school regressiontest).If -n is not specified then a random node in the cluster is chosen at the beginning of each loop.If --norecovery is specified then recovery type tests will NOT run (ie mmshutdown, mmexpelnode).If --nosnapshots is specified then snapshot tests will NOT run.If --norestorefs is specified then mmrestorefs and checksums will be run.If --noclones is specified then clone related tests will NOT run.If --nofilesets is specified then fileset tests will NOT run.If --nosobar is specified then mmimgbackup and mmimgrestore, sobar tests, will NOT run.If --no is specified then do not prompt after a failure (old school regressiontest).If --mmcrfs-undoc is specified then some undocumented mmcrfs options will be run in addition. These options are -i and --dir-block-size.If --snc is specified then all the snc flags on mmcrfs will be utilized.If --skipquotas is provided then we omit quota commandsIf --skipsmallfs is used then the creation and munipulation of the small 1 disk file system will be skipped. This is useful for testing SNC (and others) since the small file has nothing to do with SNC.If --runonlysmallfs is used then the creation and munipulation of the small 1 disk file system will be run and nothing else. This will be done for only one iterationprintlongusage: ./regressiontest[1916]: it's: not found--forcediffblocksizes is used to run with different data and metadata block sizes in newly created small filesystem.If --tokencheck is specified then each time a return code is checked, gpfs will run a diagnostic, tsfsctl fsname --token-check, to make sure tokens are in a good state.The default for -l is 100. If 0 given then skips down to bottom.-p is the number of seconds between commands. On a stressed system this should not be too low. Default is 25 seconds.-m is the number of seconds to wait for the mount/unmount commands to finish. Default is 60 seconds.-w is the Windows drive letter for the temporary file system. Default is G.--time adds the "time" command to all commands.-M gathers selected commands on linux to aid in memory leak detection. Find in /log/$date.-x says to run offline mmfsck after major commands. Either no stress can be running or use --startstress and --stopstress.--startstress is used in concert with --stopstress. It needs to be a command in quotes or a file/program that starts stress at the beginning of each loop or after the unmount for mmfsck. Be aware that the equal sign (=) is required.--stopstress is used in concert with --startstress. It needs to be a command in quotes or a file/program that kills or stops the stress started with --startstress. Be aware that the equal sign (=) is required.Instead of using startstress/stopstress, you can use the --gerontionCommands and --gerontionFlags flags to specify the gerontion commands and flags to use. Note that --startstress and stopstress is incompatible with --gerontionCommands and --gerontionFlags--tracescope is used for the mmdsh mmtrace command. It is the scope of that command. It is useful to specify a value so that traces are cut for multicluster problems. The default is "all".--mmdefragfs is used to run mmdefragfs after populateFS to make full block available. it is useful for the small file system with a small size of disk.--bypassfsckprompt is used to pass -xb option to the mmfsck call. Useful if you are hitting questions during mmfsck related to the environment setup.--4kdisk is used to test GPFS 4k-aligned file system--express is used to test GPFS Express Edition installs.--noxa is used to ignore the -xa flag. It is on by default. All extended features like - ILM, AFM, CNFS tests will be automatically disabled. Examples:1. regressiontest -f fs1 Runs regressiontest against fs1. Disks and node are chosen randomly at the beginning of each loop and runs forever. 1a regressiontest -f fs1 --gerontionCommands tortdir,ioMixer --gerontionFlags="--mmap --dio" Runs regressiontest against fs1 and handles gerontion IO automatically 2. regressiontest -f fs1 -d gpfs1nsd -s gpfs2nsd -n c154n01 --norecovery Runs command regression using disks gpfs1nsd and gpfs2nsd and c154n01 in all loops. No randomness. No recovery commands will run meaning stress will stay running on c154n01. 3. regressiontest -f fs1 -x --startstress="/u/gpfstest/bin/gerontion -N /nodes -F fs1 mkfiles" --stopstress="/u/gpfstest/bin/gerontion_killer mkfiles" Runs offline fsck against fs1 after major commands. Runs mkfiles stress which is stopped before fsck and started again afterwards. Since a command string is given for stress, the quotes are not optional. 4. regressiontest -f fs1 --startstress=/u/steve/bin/startscript --stopstress=/u/steve/bin/stopscript -l 10 Starts stress using startscript at the start of each of the 10 loops. Uses stopscript to stop and clean up stress at the end of each of the 10 loops. 5. regressiontest -f fs1 -l 1 -p 2 This command is useful for verifying ptfs or builds. It runs through all the commands one time and only pauses 2 seconds between the commands rather than the usual 25 seconds. This gives just enough time for the mmsdrfs to be copied around. 6. regressiontest -f fs2 | tee /u/steve/tmp/regressiontest.fs2.out 2>&1 Same as example 1, but pipes output to a file and the screen. This allows user to still be able to hit y or n in case it dies at an ok time. 7. nohup regressiontest -f fs3 --no > /u/steve/tmp/regressiontest.fs3.out 2>&1 Same as example 6, but pipes output to a file. The --no is required if using nohup. The help output of gerontion # /u/gpfstest/bin/gerontion -hdirname /u/gpfstest/binAdding /u/gpfstest/stress/gerontion to INCAdding /u/gpfstest/bin to INCCreating local logdir: /log/gerontion.201222.062802arguments:Logging gerontion startup to /log/gerontion.201222.062802/gerontionLog.201222.062802.c550f5u28No IO flags provided, I am turning on randomFlagsYou requested random flags. Flags enabled are:dio 0 mmap 1 aio 1 vio 0 dmapi 0 punchHoleIO 0 fsync 0 clone 0 prealloc 1 compress 1 ea 0 privateFiles 0 Description: A wrapper that will launch stress on the requested nodes. There are helper utilities in /u/gpfstest/stress/gerontion Usage: ./gerontion -N NODES -F FS_NAME [OPTIONS] PROGRAMS General options: -N NODES Nodes to use. n1,n2,... or a nodefile -F FS_NAME FS name or mountpoint -f PATH Relative path within the FS to run programs -w Exclude Windows nodes -v Verbose. Prints out all commands being done -s Silent. Prints minimal output. Good for scripting. -h help; prints out this help message Fancier options: --oldFileset Run programs in their own dependent filesets --logdir Output logs go in this directory; default is /log/gerontion.201222.062802 --newFileset Run programs in their own independent filesets --strace Run all programs through strace or truss (on aix). You must have already installed strace or truss. --ubi Runs a particular workload for a ubi critsit, (may 2019) --resume <runID> Restart this prior gerontion run. No need to provide any additional arguments Some perl programs don't resume properly. Also, if you have deleted the files being used, this will fail --traceNode localNode,remNode1,... Cut traces with mmdsh from these nodes. Use with remote cluster(s) or NFS clients on error. Provide one node per mmdsh-able cluster By default, we cut traces on the local cluster. --die Exit before actually launching the programs. Debugging aid --comment STRING Annotate your gerontion runs --nodeExclude NODES Do not use these nodes, even if they are given by -N Controlling program behavior: --randomUsers Create or chown files using the pfsXXX users from userAdd. Default setting: 1. For <dirsplit iago ioMixer smallSeq cantor> --burst X Run bursts of I/O interspersed with sleeps of up to X seconds. For <cdata fstest driver thrasher renameSlosh cacheFiller dataInode crDelRddir untar sparsedir tribunal readdirMsg cloneVM kentStress ioMixer mixedMeterIO msgStress aclStress growShrinkDir dirFragmentStress compileStress gpfs_fsscan kgnrdwr cloneloop cloneTree mkfrag mkfiles> Better mirrors some customer workloads, avoids overloading your cluster --nfsSafe Do IO in an NFS safe fashion. For <dioReg fsscan driver ioMixer dirsplit kentStress mixedMeterIO smallSeq bufferMixer dirslave> --kafka Programs should generate output tuned to help debug kafka. For <dirsplit driver bigfile dioReg ioMixer smallSeq qstress kodak dataInode renameSlosh cacheFiller thrasher> --watch Programs should generate output tuned to help debug Watch Folders. For <dirsplit driver bigfile dioReg ioMixer smallSeq qstress kodak dataInode renameSlosh cacheFiller thrasher> --privateFiles Nodes do I/O to their own files. For <ioMixer smallSeq dioReg dataInode iago negative_iago bigfile> For testing the cached fastpath, so it also uses smaller blocksize and fewer files --light Run programs with minimal intensity Controlling I/O characteristics: --fsync Use fsync (O_SYNC, fsync, fdatasync). For <iago ioMixer kentStress cloneVM msgStress gpfsDriver thrasher dataInode mixedMeterIO cdata smallSeq kodak> --dio Use O_DIRECT. For <iago dirsplit tribunal cloneVM kentStress fsscan mixedMeterIO dioReg ioMixer smallSeq kodak cantor> --randdio Use O_DIRECT randomly. For <iago dirsplit> --mmap Use mmap. For <fstest detectcorrupt cdata tortdir iozone dirsplit truncbane iago cloneVM kentStress fsscan mixedMeterIO smallSeq driver leveller mmapCache cantor> --disableMMap Never use mmap. For <checkdata> --randmmap Use mmap randomly. For <iago> --aio Use AIO. For <kentStress cloneVM fsscan mixedMeterIO dioReg smallSeq kodak leveller> For "true AIO", use with --dio. See fvt_file.h for details --vio Use VIO. For <kentStress cloneVM fsscan mixedMeterIO kodak cantor> --dmapiIO Use dmapi IO (dm_read/write_invis). For <ioMixer> You do not need a DMAPI-enabled FS. DO NOT USE UNLESS YOU KNOW WHAT YOU'RE DOING (cf. CMVC.1019071). --punchHoleIO Use dmapi hole punching. For <ioMixer> You do not need a DMAPI-enabled FS DO NOT USE UNLESS YOU KNOW WHAT YOU'RE DOING (See 977646 for warning) --clone Clone stress. For <detectcorrupt mkfiles kgnrdwr tortdir mkfrag cloneTree iago dirsplit truncbane> --ea EA stress. For <dbench iago dirsplit driver ioMixer dioReg smallSeq kodak dataInode leveller cantor> --acl ACL stress. For <iago dirsplit aclStress ioMixer driver smallSeq dioReg kodak dataInode thrasher> --prealloc Use gpfs_prealloc. For <driver tribunal iago> --percentFallocate: requires --prealloc. For iago only. What percent of the time we should use fallocate vs gpfs_prealloc --compress Use GPFS compression. For <ioMixer dioReg driver tribunal mixedMeterIO truncbane iago dataInode dirsplit smallSeq kodak leveller cantor> --normalIO Programs which default to random IO forms will use normal IO instead. For <kentStress cloneVM mixedMeterIO> --all Enable all flavors of I/O Clones, declones, compression, eas, prealloc, aio, vio, and a 50-50 pick between mmap and dio --randomFlags A random selection of I/O flavors If you provide no flavors of IO (including --normalIO), this is the default Tuning specific programs: tortdir --overflowOnly --tortdirMaxFiles X readsnap --readsnapOnePass: read through the snapshot list only once dirsplit --inodeCreate --dirsplitVerbose X iago --iago{IO|EA|ACL|Clone}Thread X --iagoVerbose X --iagoMaxBlocks X --iagoBlockSize X truncbane --truncbaneVerbose X --truncbaneThread X aclStress --aclStressVerbose X blast --blastThread X --blastSmallFiles bigfile --bigfileThreads X qstress --qstressThreads X --qStressDataPerNode X --qstressInodesPerNode X --qstressUser username --qstressThreads X ioMixer --ioMixerThreads X --ioMixerVerifyFiles N --ioMixerNoVerifyFiles N --ioMixerPercentDIO X --ioMixerBlocksize X --ioMixerMaxFilesize X cdata --cdataAppendMode <makes cdata do mostly appends/shrinks Allowed programs: cdata dbench fstest blast locktest iozone cthon detectcorrupt mkfiles dirstress kgnrdwr tortdir checkdata trunctest mkfrag cloneTree iago negative_iago readSnap dirsplit fgdl_dirsplit truncbane driver untar sparsedir handle thrasher tribunal fsscan renameSlosh cacheFiller cloneloop dataInode crDelRddir shadowWriter clonepy bigfile aclStress gpfs_fsscan racer aclsforall growShrinkDir dirFragmentStress readdirMsg msgStress cloneVM kentStress ioMixer dioReg compileStress mixedMeterIO dirRacer smallSeq qstress kodak dirslave seeker singleAppend leveller mmapCache cantor NB fstest and blast are the only ones that run on windows nodes --randomCmd X In addition to any named programs, start X randomly chosen programs --exclude "P1 P2 ..." For randomCmd, never use these programs. Magic Keywords: autotest ==> dirstress, kgnrdwr, and tortdir light ==> cdata, locktest, and checkdata. With minimal intensity. Examples: gerontion -N /nodes -F fs0 dbench cdata fstest gpfsperf Run these programs on the nodes in /nodes into FS fs0 gerontion -N vmip101,vmip102 -F gpfs1 -f rundir --randomCmd 3 --randomFlags Run 3 programs on these 2 nodes into FS gpfs1 subdir rundir. Use random I/O modes. gerontion ... -c /tmp/newCommands.pl autotest Run the autotest suite using the commands specified in /tmp/newCommands.pl gerontion ... -w -F /NFS_mount_point fstest Run fstest on non-Windows nodes into this NFS mount point gerontion ... --nodeExclude linuxnodes --light ... Exclude linux nodes from this light workload The output of mmbackupreg.pl # ./mmbackupreg.pl -husage:mmbackupreg.pl {-f FSNAME} [-N {Node[,Node...]}] [-g sharedirectory] [-l LOGDIR] [-L loopnum] [-m multiThreadNum] [-C] [-v All|{1[,2,3...]}] [--testSnap] [--noRestore] [--cleanall] [-q]. [-s tsmserver1[,tsmserver2]]. # default: servers extracted from dsm.sys -f FSNAME: GPFS Filesystem Name. -l LOGDIR: directory for log; default is /log. -L loopnum: loop times; default is 1. -N Node[,Node]: worker nodes that will run parallel instances of the backup process. -g sharedirectory: directory used for worker nodes share temporary files. -C: clear Files/Dirs after complete test cases. -v: choice cases you want to run. default, all cases will be run. -m: multiThreadNum: number of threads mmbackup transfered to mmapplypolicy. --noRestore: just for a tsm bug to not restore files when selinux enabled. --cleanall: remove all old subdirs below mountdir that mmbackupreg.pl ever created. -q: add -q option for each mmbackup execution to rebuild shadow everytime CASES: case1: mmbackup basic functions test, also rebuilding shadow database file case2: mmbackup test cases for fileset. case3: mmbackup filesystem with snapshot. case4: mmbackup test cases for EAs. case5: mmbackup with exclude/include rules. case6: mmbackup files with ugly names, utf-8 characters and long names. case7: mmbackup a mass of small files. case8: ctime change test. case9: mmbackup files with ACLs. case10: Check mmbackup response to an unmounted file system or to missing TSM client. The output of hsmreg.pl # ./hsmreg.plusage:/u/gpfstest/regression/backup_archive/TSM/hsmreg.pl {-f FSNAME} [-s TSM-SERVER] [-l LOGDIR] [-L loopnum] [-T] [-C] [-v All|{1[,2,3...]}]. -f FSNAME: GPFS Filesystem Name, ensure the fs is added to TSM server first. -s TSM-SERVER: The TSM-server must have a valid stanza in dsm.sys file. optional if there is only one stanza in dsm.sys -l LOGDIR: directory for log write; default is /log. -L loopnum: loop times; default is 1. -C: clear Files/Dirs after complete test cases. -p Use predefined test file fill pattern - use this if the default (random) is too slow. -t <sec>: custom timeout for automigration and daemon restart on slow nodes. -T: multiprocess mode. -v: choice cases you want to run. default, all cases will be run. --cleanall: remove all old subdirs below mountdir that hsmreg ever created CASES: case1 : dsmmigrate/dsmrecall general files/dirs. [002]~ case2 : dsmmigrate/dsmrecall files with EAs/Immutability/AppendOnly. [002]~ case3 : migrate/recall using policies. [002] case4 : excluding file(s) from migration by rule, recall on read/write. [002] + reconciliation[013] case5 : preparation and parallel processing of file lists [005] case6 : moves migrated files within and among filesets (root, dependent, independent) case7 : backup and restore a resident, migrated, premigrated file (stub restore) case8 : whole automigration: filling data to upper threshold, check migrated, premigrated files case9 : Migration using exclude via dsm.sys for files and directories case10: A specialized exclusion test (excl. by rule) exactly covering CQ S1060335 case11: Migration + low level backup / restore of a file with direct I/O and EAs case12: dsmmigrate/dsmc ba/restore files with weird names case13: Using different options of the policy engine for migration case14: Check if killed HSM daemons get automatically restarted ('FOR FILESET','SHOW','ACTION','WHEN'). case15: Remove and restore HSM management on a (GPFS) file system case16: Check the presence of necessary HSM callbacks

entry.title: How to setup a GPFS multicluster environment
entry.content: A GPFS cluster can configure mixed OS as nodes, and also can mount a remote GPFS file system. This article is to setup a multicluster for regression test.There are two different cluster roles on a multicluster environment, server cluster(aka owning cluster or home cluster) and client cluster(aka accessing cluster). The client cluster is the one that mounts the remote file system from the server cluster.Prerequisites Two existing GPFS clusters, at least one file system mounted on the server cluster. The package gpfs.gskit must be installed on both clusters.Steps to setup a multicluster environmentGenerate authentication key files on both clusters Run below commands on both clusters to generate new key files # mmshutdown -a# mmauth genkey new# mmlsconfig | grep cipherList // Check if cipherList is specified or not# mmchconfig cipherList=AUTHONLY // Specify cipherList if not set yet# mmstartup -a Copy the new generated public key files(/var/mmfs/ssl/id_rsa_new.pub) to remote cluster. For example, use scp command to copy the one of server cluster to client cluster, and vice versa. Add the client cluster public key to the server cluster(server cluster)# mmauth add <client_cluster> -k <the_public_key_of_client_cluster>Example:# mmauth add rhpower.GPFS -k 613id_rsa_new.pubmmauth: Propagating the cluster configuration data to all affected nodes.mmauth: Command successfully completedAdd the server cluster on the client cluster(client cluster)# mmremotecluster add <server_cluster> -k <the_public_key_of_server_cluster> -n <nodes_of_server_cluster>Example:# mmremotecluster add rhsles.GPFS -k ~/628id_rsa_new.pub -n c550f6u28,c550f5u28,c550f5u31mmremotecluster: Command successfully completedmmremotecluster: Propagating the cluster configuration data to all affected nodes. This is an asynchronous process.Grant the access to the file system of server cluster(server cluster)# mmauth grant <client_cluster> -f <file_system>Example:# mmauth grant rhpower.GPFS -f fs2mmauth: Granting cluster rhpower.GPFS access to file system fs2: access type rw; root credentials will not be remapped.mmauth: Propagating the cluster configuration data to all affected nodes.mmauth: Command successfully completed Define the remote file system on client cluster(client cluster)# mmremotefs add <new_local_file_system> -f <remote_file_system> -C <server_cluster> -A noExample:# mmremotefs add 628_fs2 -f fs2 -C rhsles.GPFS -A nommremotefs: Propagating the cluster configuration data to all affected nodes. This is an asynchronous process.Mount the file system on the client cluster(client cluster)# mmmount <new_local_file_system> -aExample:# mmmount 628_fs2 -aReferencesMulticluster from GpfsWikiAccessing a remote GPFS file system from Knowledge CenterSetting up a multicluster environment using General Parallel File System

entry.title: YUM commands with network error code 400
entry.content: When I tried to run some yum commands on a testing node, can see the warning “Network error code: 400” every time.Environment Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.xIssue YUM commands reported “Network error code: 400” every time. # yum repolistLoaded plugins: product-id, search-disabled-repos, subscription-managerNetwork error code: 400 <<<<< Resolution Cleaning the subscription-manager data, clears old certificate files and corrupt data. # subscription-manager cleanAll local data removed # subscription-manager status+-------------------------------------------+ System Status Details+-------------------------------------------+Overall Status: Unknown Diagnostic Steps Traceback found in /var/log/rhsm/rhsm.log file: 2021-01-08 03:33:15,841 [INFO] yum:18651:MainThread @connection.py:830 - Connection built: host=subscription.rhsm.redhat.com port=443 handler=/subscription auth=identity_cert ca_dir=/etc/rhsm/ca/ verify=False2021-01-08 03:33:15,845 [INFO] yum:18651:MainThread @connection.py:830 - Connection built: host=subscription.rhsm.redhat.com port=443 handler=/subscription auth=identity_cert ca_dir=/etc/rhsm/ca/ verify=False2021-01-08 03:33:16,386 [ERROR] yum:18651:MainThread @connection.py:631 - Response: 4002021-01-08 03:33:16,386 [ERROR] yum:18651:MainThread @connection.py:632 - JSON parsing error: No JSON object could be decoded ReferenceSubscription-manager command fails with “NetworkException: Network error code: 400”

entry.title: Upgrading RHEL without RHSM from 7.9 to 8.2
entry.content: Almost all of our testing machines are accessed remotely, so you have to patch or upgrade some of them to the specific versions some day. Now, I have a chance to upgrade a node from RHEL 7.9 to 8.2.Prerequisites An existing RHEL 7.9 with custom repositories, and a custom repository file of RHEL 8.2. The custom repositories should be including: RHEL 7 Base (to provide the latest RHEL 7 packages)RHEL 7 Extras (to provide the Leapp utility and its dependencies)RHEL 8 BaseOSRHEL 8 AppStream Ensure your system does not use more than one Network Interface Card (NIC) with a name based on the prefix used by the kernel (eth). If have, can follow up this article to change it. If the root filesystem is XFS, ensure its ftype is not 0, otherwise the upgrade will hit this known issue.Procedures Ensure you have the system locale set to en_US.UTF-8: # cat /etc/locale.conf Update all packages to the latest RHEL 7 version if not # yum update -y Reboot the system if upgrading the kernel # reboot Install the Leapp utility # yum install -y leapp leapp-repository Download additional required data files “leapp-data12.tar.gz” from Red Hat, and extract them in the /etc/leapp/files/ directory. Perform the pre-upgrade phase # leapp preupgrade --no-rhsm --enablerepo repository_id1 --enablerepo repository_id2 ... Example:# leapp preupgrade --no-rhsm --enablerepo baseos --enablerepo appstream Examine the report in the /var/log/leapp/leapp-report.txt file, and manually resolve all the reported problems which marking as inhibitor, and provide answers to each question required by Leapp. # leapp answer --section remove_pam_pkcs11_module_check.confirm=True Perform the upgrade phase if the leapp report all is GREEN. # leapp upgrade --no-rhsm --enablerepo repository_id1 --enablerepo repository_id2 ... Example:# leapp upgrade --no-rhsm --enablerepo baseos --enablerepo appstream Reboot the system, Leapp upgrades all packages and automatically reboots to the RHEL 8 system, it will take about 70 minutes on this phase. Once the system can be accessed, verifying the system state. # cat /etc/redhat-releaseRed Hat Enterprise Linux release 8.2 (Ootpa) # uname -r4.18.0-193.el8.x86_64 Perform the additional packages update # yum update --bugfix --enhancement --security Update SSCA DB with the new OS version information if the node was registered in SSCA. ReferencesUPGRADING FROM RHEL 7 TO RHEL 8Upgrading from RHEL 7 to RHEL 8 with Leapp and BOOM

entry.title: How to change network device naming from eth to eno on Linux
entry.content: There are different naming schemes (e.g. eno1, ens1, enp2s0 and so on) for interface naming on Linux world. RHEL 8.x doesn’t support ethX naming during upgrading from RHEL 7.x, so you need to change it before upgrading from RHEL 7.x if have.Prerequisites An existing RHEL 7.x with network interface naming ethX. The OS have installed the package biosdevname.Procedures Open the /etc/default/grub file and find the GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX variable, add “biosdevname=1” as kernel parameter values. Example:# cat /etc/default/grubGRUB_TIMEOUT=5GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR="$(sed 's, release .*$,,g' /etc/system-release)"GRUB_DEFAULT=savedGRUB_DISABLE_SUBMENU=trueGRUB_TERMINAL_OUTPUT="console"GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="crashkernel=auto rd.lvm.lv=vg_c550f3dxn04/lv_root rd.lvm.lv=vg_c550f3dxn04/lv_swap biosdevname=1 rhgb quiet"GRUB_DISABLE_RECOVERY="true" If have “net.ifnames=0” on the variable GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX, please remove it too. Rebuild the /boot/grub2/grub.cfg file # grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg View the current device name, for example eth0 here. # nmcli connection showNAME UUID TYPE DEVICESystem eth0 5fb06bd0-0bb0-7ffb-45f1-d6edd65f3e03 ethernet eth0eth1 e4290b04-3dc8-4759-ae0d-35dc1e38fabd ethernet --ib0 ed2118ea-8117-4935-a6f2-746aa9e5f490 infiniband --usb0 b7becf20-7a79-4209-899d-33d8a39f47e5 ethernet -- Modify the device name to eno1, and reboot the system. # nmcli connection modify "System eth0" connection.interface-name eno1# reboot After the OS bootup, verify the device name. # nmcli connection show# ifconfig | grep flags Examples:# nmcli connection showNAME UUID TYPE DEVICESystem eth0 5fb06bd0-0bb0-7ffb-45f1-d6edd65f3e03 ethernet eno1eth1 e4290b04-3dc8-4759-ae0d-35dc1e38fabd ethernet --ib0 ed2118ea-8117-4935-a6f2-746aa9e5f490 infiniband --usb0 b7becf20-7a79-4209-899d-33d8a39f47e5 ethernet -- # ifconfig | grep flagseno1: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 1500eno2: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 1500enp0s29f1u2: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 1500lo: flags=73<UP,LOOPBACK,RUNNING> mtu 65536 ReferencesConsistent Network Device Naming from Red HatIs it safe to set net.ifnames=0 in RHEL7 and RHEL8?If RHEL 7.x used ethX, you can see below risk on leapp report while upgrading to RHEL 8.x:Risk Factor: high (inhibitor)Title: Unsupported network configurationSummary: Detected multiple network interfaces using unstable kernel names (e.g. eth0, eth1). Upgrade process can not continue because stability of names can not be guaranteed. Please read the article at https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4067471 for more information.

entry.title: How to configure NFS-Ganesha without a CES IP
entry.content: Sometime we are not convenient to configure a CES IP for protocol node, due to lack of additional IP resource or no physical links on additional ethernet ports(especially remote machines).This article is to configure NFS-Ganesha without a CES IP, it should be fine for most NFS relevant testing.Prerequisites An existing GPFS cluster, and have filesystem mounted. The NFS relevant packages were installed, which under /usr/lpp/mmfs/<5.x.y.z>/ganesha_rpms.Steps to configure NFS-Ganesha Configure the CES shared root if not yet # mmshutdown -a# mmchconfig cesSharedRoot=<shared_root_path># mmstartup -a Example:# mmchconfig cesSharedRoot=/gpfs/fs1 Enable a protocol node # mmgetstate -a // Ensure that all nodes state are "active"# mmchnode --ces-enable -N Node1 Create and link a fileset for NFS # mmlsmount all // Ensure the existing filesystem mounted# mmcrfileset <FileSystem> <fileset> --inode-space new# mmlinkfileset <FileSystem> <fileset> [-J JunctionPath] Examples:# mmcrfileset fs1 nfs_fileset --inode-space=new# mmlinkfileset fs1 nfs_fileset -J /gpfs/fs1/home/nfstest > In above example, you need to create the directory /gpfs/fs1/home/ firstly if not exist. Start NFS service and set up the authentication method # mmces service enable NFS# systemctl daemon-reload# mmuserauth service create --data-access-method file --type userdefined Create an NFS export # mmnfs export add <exported_path># mmnfs export list Examples:# mmnfs export add /gpfs/fs1/home/nfstest/ -c "*(Access_Type=RW,Squash=no_root_squash)"# mmnfs export list -n /gpfs/fs1/home/nfstest/ Remove the NFS export after testing # mmnfs export remove <exported_path> Example:# mmnfs export remove /gpfs/fs1/home/nfstest/ ReferencesNFS Installation from GpfsWikiConfiguring the CES and protocol configuration from Knowledge CenterGPFS commands reference from Knowledge Center

The node have installed GUI, can remote access GUI via VNC if can’t physical access. The node have installed the required software, refer to Software requirements for more information.Steps to install/configure TSM serverCreate user and group id for the TSM server instance Run below commands to create user tsminst1 and its group # groupadd tsmsrvrs -g 500# useradd -d /home/tsminst1 -m -u 500 -g 500 -s /bin/bash tsminst1# passwd tsminst1 # ppslab Extract and run the TSM installer tool Extract the downloaded binary file # chmod +x SP_8.1.11_LIN86_SERSTG_AGT_ML.bin# ./SP_8.1.11_LIN86_SERSTG_AGT_ML.bin inflating: repository/plugins/com.tivoli.dsm.stagent.moreinfo_8.1.11.202011031146.jar inflating: repository/repository.config inflating: repository/repository.xml creating: .input/ inflating: .input/installnew32.xml inflating: .input/installnew64.xml inflating: .input/install_response.xml creating: input/ inflating: input/install_response_sample.xml inflating: input/uninstall_response_sample.xml inflating: input/update_response_sample.xml inflating: im32/post-install.xml inflating: im64/post-install.xml inflating: README.htm Run the TSM installer tool # ./install.shGUI failed to start. entry.title: How to install VNC Server on RHEL 7.x
entry.content: Some testing might use GUI to operate tasks, or some configuration wizard need GUI to proceed, but we often remote access the servers.This article will guide you how to install VNC Server and configure it for RHEL 7.x environment.Prerequisites A linux server which installed Environment Groups “Server with GUI” The linux default run level is graphical, firewall is disabled.Steps to install/configure VNC Server Verify the installed group list # yum grouplistInstalled Environment Groups: Server with GUI --> Here identify this OS installed GUIAvailable Environment Groups: Minimal Install Infrastructure Server File and Print Server Cinnamon Desktop MATE Desktop Basic Web Server Virtualization Host Install GUI environment if need by following commands: # yum groupinstall -y "Server with GUI"# systemctl get-default# systemctl set-default graphical.target# reboot Install VNC Server via YUM # yum install -y tigervnc-server Configure VNC Server # cp /lib/systemd/system/vncserver@.service /etc/systemd/system/.# vi /etc/systemd/system/vncserver@.serviceReplace <USER> with the actual user name(e.g. root) # systemctl daemon-reload# vncpasswd // Set the password used to access VNC desktops Start VNC Server # systemctl start vncserver@:1# systemctl enable vncserver@:1 // Optional# systemctl status vncserver@:1 Reference MacOS install a VNC viewer to access the VNC Server # brew install --cask tigervnc-viewer

entry.title: How to install a PTF build on an ESS environment
entry.content: To verify a defect, I have to run mmchrecoverygroup with –active option, but that is only working on an ESS environment after trying different configuration for days.Prerequisites An ESS environment with existing configuration All nodes in the cluster can mount /u/gpfstest and /u/imagesSteps to install a PTF build Mount /u/gpfstest and /u/images # mount -t nfs it2n01:/u/gpfstest /u/gpfstest# mount -t nfs it2n01:/u/images /u/images Find the specific PTF image location (e.g. 5.0.5.5 here), extract it. # /u/images/SPECTRUM_SCALE/5.0.5_tac505/Spectrum_Scale_Product/PTFS/ptf5/SE_Packages/Daily/latest/x86_64/Spectrum_Scale_Erasure_Code-5.0.5.5-x86_64-Linux-install --silent Shutdown the GPFS daemon on the node # /usr/lpp/mmfs/bin/mmshutdown Install the rpm packages # /u/gpfstest/GNR/bin/installgnr.sh /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/gpfs_rpms Startup the GPFS daemon on the node # /usr/lpp/mmfs/bin/mmstartup Repeat above steps on all the remaining nodes References (Example) One-line command to install GPFS 5.0.5.5 on one node: # mount -t nfs it2n01:/u/gpfstest /u/gpfstest; mount -t nfs it2n01:/u/images /u/images; /u/images/SPECTRUM_SCALE/5.0.5_tac505/Spectrum_Scale_Product/PTFS/ptf5/SE_Packages/Daily/latest/x86_64/Spectrum_Scale_Erasure_Code-5.0.5.5-x86_64-Linux-install --silent; /usr/lpp/mmfs/bin/mmshutdown; sleep 5; /u/gpfstest/GNR/bin/installgnr.sh /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/gpfs_rpms; sleep 5; /usr/lpp/mmfs/bin/mmstartup; sleep 10; /usr/lpp/mmfs/bin/mmgetstate -a Similar Output of above one-line command(exclude two mount commands): Extracting License Acceptance Process Tool to /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5 ...tail -n +641 /u/images/SPECTRUM_SCALE/5.0.5_tac505/Spectrum_Scale_Product/PTFS/ptf5/SE_Packages/Daily/latest/x86_64/Spectrum_Scale_Erasure_Code-5.0.5.5-x86_64-Linux-install | tar -C /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5 -xvz --exclude=installer --exclude=*_rpms --exclude=*_debs --exclude=*rpm --exclude=*tgz --exclude=*deb --exclude=*tools* 1> /dev/null Installing JRE ... If directory /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5 has been created or was previously created during another extraction,.rpm, .deb, and repository related files in it (if there were) will be removed to avoid conflicts with the ones being extracted. tail -n +641 /u/images/SPECTRUM_SCALE/5.0.5_tac505/Spectrum_Scale_Product/PTFS/ptf5/SE_Packages/Daily/latest/x86_64/Spectrum_Scale_Erasure_Code-5.0.5.5-x86_64-Linux-install | tar -C /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5 --wildcards -xvz ibm-java*tgz 1> /dev/nulltar -C /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/ -xzf /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/ibm-java*tgz Invoking License Acceptance Process Tool .../usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/ibm-java-x86_64-80/jre/bin/java -cp /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/LAP_HOME/LAPApp.jar com.ibm.lex.lapapp.LAP -l /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/LA_HOME -m /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5 -s /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5 -t 5 License Agreement Terms accepted. install a cluster manually: Use the gpfs packages located within /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/gpfs_<rpms/debs> To upgrade an existing cluster using the Spectrum Scale Install Toolkit: 1) Copy your old clusterdefinition.txt file to the new /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/installer/configuration/ location 2) Review and update the config: /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/installer/spectrumscale config update 3) (Optional) Update the toolkit to reflect the current cluster config: /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/installer/spectrumscale config populate -N <node> 4) Run the upgrade: /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/installer/spectrumscale upgrade -h To add nodes to an existing cluster using the Spectrum Scale Install Toolkit: 1) Add nodes to the clusterdefinition.txt file: /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/installer/spectrumscale node add -h 2) Install GPFS on the new nodes: /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/installer/spectrumscale install -h 3) Deploy protocols on the new nodes: /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/installer/spectrumscale deploy -h To update the toolkit to reflect the current cluster config examples: /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.0.5.5/installer/spectrumscale config populate -N <node> 1) Manual updates outside of the install toolkit 2) Sync the current cluster state to the install toolkit prior to upgrade 3) Switching from a manually managed cluster to the install toolkit entry.title: How to setup ECE on an incompatible environment
entry.content: ECE configuration require SAS-attached HDD, SSD drives that use specified LSI adapters or enterprise-class NVMe drives, at least 25 Gbps bandwidth networking. Based on my previous testing in project MachineCity, it is more sensitive than NSD configuration.Unfortunately, our lab might have few supported environment for testing, so have to setup ECE on an incompatible environment.Prerequisites Passwordless SSH must be set up using the FQDN and the short name of the node. The following rpms are required to be installed: sg3_utils nvme-cli storcli (if you use SAS drives with LSI HBA) dmidecode PyYAML Steps to install ECE Extract the installation package on the installer node ONLY, can be found under it2n01:/u/images/SPECTRUM_SCALE. # ./Spectrum_Scale_Erasure_Code-5.x.y.z-x86_64-Linux-install --silent Specify the installer node and the setup type in the cluster definition file # cd /usr/lpp/mmfs/5.x.y.z/installer/# ./spectrumscale setup -s <InstallerNodeIP> -st ece Add different role nodes for ECE in the cluster definition file # ./spectrumscale node add <NodeName> -q -m -so# ./spectrumscale node add <NodeName> -a -g# ./spectrumscale node add <NodeName> -a -m -so# ./spectrumscale node list Example:# ./spectrumscale node add c550f5u01 -q -m -so Define the recovery group for ECE in the cluster definition file ## Only create one recoverygroup # ./spectrumscale recoverygroup define -N <Node1,Node2,...,NodeN> ## Create more than one recoverygroups# ./spectrumscale recoverygroup define -rg <RGName> -nc <ScaleOutNodeClassName> -N <Node1,Node2,...,NodeN> Example:# ./spectrumscale recoverygroup define -rg rg_1 -nc nc_1 -N c550f5u01,c550f5u02,c550f5u03,c550f5u04 (Optionals) Configure cluster name, disable callhome and so on. # ./spectrumscale config gpfs -c <clusterName># ./spectrumscale config gpfs --ephemeral_port_range 60000-61000# ./spectrumscale callhome disable Perform environment prechecks before issuing install command # ./spectrumscale install --precheck --skip no-ece-check Create recoverygroup using mmvdisk ## Before ECE 5.0.5.4# mmvdisk rg create --rg <RGName> --nc <RelevantNodeClassName> -v no ## Start from ECE 5.0.5.4, MUST turn off "strict pdisk slot location" checking firstly# echo 999 | mmchconfig nsdRAIDStrictPdiskSlotLocation=0 -i# mmvdisk rg create --rg <RGName> --nc <RelevantNodeClassName> -v no Example:# mmvdisk rg create --rg rg_1 --nc nc_1 -v no Perform the installation toolkit installation procedure # ./spectrumscale install --skip no-ece-check Using mmvdisk to create vdisk sets for additional parameters # mmvdisk vdiskset define --vdisk-set <vdisksetName> --recovery-group <RGName> --code <RaidCode> --block-size <BlockSize> --set-size <n%> --declustered-array <DAName> --nsd-usage <NSDUsage> --storage-pool <PoolName># mmvdisk vdiskset create --vdisk-set all Examples:# mmvdisk vdiskset define --vdisk-set HDD-Data --recovery-group rg_1 --code 8+3p --block-size 16M --set-size 100% --declustered-array DA1 --nsd-usage dataonly --storage-pool data# mmvdisk vdiskset define --vdisk-set SSD-Meta --recovery-group rg_1 --code 8+3p --block-size 2M --set-size 100% --declustered-array DA2 --nsd-usage metadataonly --storage-pool system# mmvdisk vdiskset create --vdisk-set allOr# mmvdisk vdiskset define --vdisk-set HDD1-Data --recovery-group rg_1 --code 4+3p --block-size 4m --set-size 30% --declustered-array DA1 --nsd-usage dataonly --storage-pool data# mmvdisk vdiskset define --vdisk-set HDD2-Data --recovery-group rg_2 --code 4+3p --block-size 8m --set-size 70% --declustered-array DA1 --nsd-usage dataonly --storage-pool data# mmvdisk vdiskset define --vdisk-set SSD1-Meta --recovery-group rg_1 --code 4+2p --block-size 1M --set-size 50% --declustered-array DA2 --nsd-usage metadataonly --storage-pool system# mmvdisk vdiskset define --vdisk-set SSD2-Meta --recovery-group rg_1 --code 4+2p --block-size 2M --set-size 50% --declustered-array DA2 --nsd-usage metadataonly --storage-pool system# mmvdisk vdiskset create --vdisk-set all RAID code ‘4+3p’ requires 7 non-spare pdisks, ‘mmvdisk vdiskset create’ will be failed if not enough spare pdisks. Using mmvdisk to create file system and mount it to all nodes # mmvdisk vdiskset create --file-system <FSName> --vdisk-set <VSName># mmmount all -a Example:# mmvdisk filesystem create --file-system ptf_FS1 --vdisk-set SSD-Meta,HDD-Data --mmcrfs -T /ptf_FS1 ReferencesThe Knowledge Center of ECE 5.1.0Turn off “strict pdisk slot location” checkingSpectrum Scale Erasure Code Edition (From SSUG)

entry.title: The procedures to relocate lab devices
entry.content: There were dozens of idle devices(including servers/switches/monitors/disks and so on) in Shanghai after RA(Resource Action), which were requested to relocate to Beijing under management decision. I was assigned to handle this project(not a real established project, but I would handle it as a small project).Start to collect the available devices informationIf there is an available pool list, can save a lot of time. What you only need is to check its location and some information(e.g. Serial, quantity) correct or not. Otherwise, you should take some time to collect such information and document then print them on papers.Verify the available devices healthyIf the available devices were offline, you have better to power on it and confirm if can pass POST at least, you can replace the failed parts too if have spare parts.Label the devices which will be shippedOnce the devices which will be shipped, one good option is to label them. Not only the device itself, but also the cables which will be shipped together.Pull the devices from the RackHave better to borrow one small wagon from 2F pantry, at least two persons pull a 2U server from the rail of the rack, then put the heavy devices to the small wagon one by one. Then pile up the devices on a open area on the lab.##The process of PR/POGet the onsite truck number one day earlier from the logistic contact, then call company reception@69023001, tell the information and ask to inform property company, otherwise the entrance guard will not allow the truck entering the AIsland park.After packing all things, go to reception(1F) and get a release permit, fill it and get the relevant persons to sign it.

entry.title: Red Hat Certifications and Red Hat Partner OPEN courses
entry.content: IBMers are able to pursue full Red Hat Certifications by purchasing a Red Hat Learning Subscription Standard for $1000/person/year (this is chargeable to your department or to your funding IBM entity).Red Hat Learning Subscription(RHLS for short) Standard Overview Subscription fee ($1,000+) per person (Volume) Valid for one year (365 days) Access to ~100 courses & exams on technologies and products* Access to 52 courses on technologies and products Access to 14 development courses Access to 32 certification exams Covers 5 certification exams per person, per year Covers 2 certification exam retakes per person per year Access to hands-on labs (400+ Hours)Certification Exams example Code Certifications EX200 Red Hat Certified System Administrator EX294 Red Hat Certified Engineer EX280 Red Hat Certified Specialist in OpenShift Administration EX288 Red Hat Certified Specialist in OpenShift Application Development How to start after subscribing the RHLS Go to https://rol.redhat.com/rol/app/ with your Red Hat Network ID Click ‘Enroll’ under MY SKILLS PATHS to choose your skill path (e.g. Red Hat Certified Engineer or Red Hat Certified Specialist in OpenShift Administration), then enroll it. Now you can start to study the relevant courses by video classroom or online training.RHLS Quick LinksRHLS DashboardRHLS CatalogRHLS Skills PathsRHLS ReportsRHLS Learning CommunityReferencesRed Hat Training Skills AssessmentGetting Ready for your Red Hat Remote ExamAvailable Remote exams listFREE Red Hat Online CoursesRed Hat offers offers free training to partners through OPEN (Online Partner Enablement Network) Self-paced learning courses leading to accreditations Accreditation: Valid for 2 years at the current place of employment To access OPEN, create a Red Hat Account Go to partner page https://www.redhat.com/en/partners/Homepage Select “Join an existing partner company” Select REGISTER for a REDHAT.COM Account Create an account with IBM Internet ID (e.g., name@us.ibm.com) Verify Email – An email verification note will be sent to you Follow the instructions in the note and verify your email address Back on partner page: https://www.redhat.com/en/partners/Homepage Select “Join an existing partner company” Select “Login to A Redhat.com Account” using credentials from step #1 Select partner type “System Integrator” E-mail will be sent to you with link & access to Red Hat OPEN portal OPEN portal URL https://partnercenter.redhat.com/Dashboard_page

entry.title: Setup Jabber after Voice Service migration
entry.content: IBM Voice Service has moved to the cloud-based Global Voice Services since December 1st. Your phone number remains the same for the existing Jabber users.Unfortunately, there is no official IT newsletter to guide us to re-configure Jabber so far, I found the login issue today and spent hours to fix it until calling IT helpdesk. Recording the solution here for your reference, which can save time in case you hit the same problem.Please note that this article is only for the existing Jabber users, not for new Jabber users.Problem Description If you always open Jabber, you might see an alert computer icon on the bottom of the Jabber window, the alert message should be “Connection to Phone Service failed.”. If you have exited Jabber, trying to launch it again, it will fail to do finding services with error “Cannot find your services automatically.” Previous Jabber username/password can’t be used now, new implementation will use SSO to login.Solutions Contact IT helpdesk(Hotline: 400-670-2255) for help, they will remote access your system and can remote fix it. Following below procedures to fix it by yourself, should be same as what IT helpdesk does. MacOS users If you have installed Big Sur(11.0.1), you need to disconnect the VPN firstly. Method One(For MacOS version < 11): Quit Jabber app; Go to Mac@IBM App Store, run the package “Re-Launch Cisco Jabber with w3ID Login”, waiting it is done; Re-login Jabber. Method Two: Quit Jabber app; Open Finder, press Command+Shift+G, go to “~/Library/Application Support/Cisco/Unified Communications/”，then delete “Jabber” folder; Copy the following command to Safari and execute it: ciscojabber://provision?ServicesDomain=ibmuc.com&ServicesDomainSsoEmailPrompt=ON&STARTUP_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED=True&RESET_JABBER=1 Jabber will be launched, then login with your w3ID and password. Windows users Uninstall current jabber, go to PC@IBM App Store, click Cisco Jabber then choose “Cisco Jabber Client” to install, then login as normal. ReferencesStart using global voice servicesOld Self Care Portal (CUCM)New Self-service Portal (Global)

entry.title: How to access Juniper/Lenovo/Brocade switches' console using Mac
entry.content: There are some idle switches in SH lab, need to verify them working or not before relocation. But I don’t have their passwords, so have to access their console and confirm.Preparation One Type-C to USB adapter One USB to RJ45 adapter One utility which can setup serial configuration(e.g. screen on MacOS or script)Usage Connect the cables between Mac(Type-C port) and switch(RJ45 console port, not mgmt port). Open Terminal on MacOS, issue the command serial (A script which uses command screen): > serial1: /dev/tty.usbserial-14430Choose serial device file > 111 : 115200 (default)2 : 96003 : 57600Choose baudrate > 2 Now insert the power cable to the switch, it will start to boot up.Appendix The script serial content #!/bin/bash# From https://blog.csdn.net/huyuan7494/article/details/82381142portname="/dev/tty.SLAB_USBtoUART"preset="$1"baudrate=115200screen_start(){ screen $portname $baudrate}if [ -n "$preset" ];then if [ "$preset" == "bst" ];then portname="/dev/tty.usbserial-A106HG1J" screen_start elif [ "$preset" == "gw" ];then portname="/dev/tty.usbserial-A106HG1J" baudrate=57600 screen_start elif [ "$preset" == "macro" ];then screen_start else echo "Preset not found.\n" fi exit 0fiarray=(`ls /dev/tty.* | grep -v "/dev/tty.SOC" | grep -v "/dev/tty.MALS" | grep -v "/dev/tty.Bluetooth-Incoming-Port"`)len=${#array[*]}i=0while [ $i -lt $len ]; doecho "$[$i+1]: ${array[$i]}"let i++doneecho -n "Choose serial device file > "read selected#echo "PORT : $selected"if [ -z "$selected" ]then selected=1fiif echo $selected | grep "^[0-9]*$" >&1then if (( $selected-1 > $len )) then exit fi portname=${array[$selected-1]} echo "1 : 115200 (default)" echo "2 : 9600" echo "3 : 57600" echo -n "Choose baudrate > " read baudrate if [ -z "$baudrate" ]; then baudrate=115200 elif [ "$baudrate" == "1" ]; then baudrate=115200 elif [ "$baudrate" == "2" ]; then baudrate=9600 elif [ "$baudrate" == "3" ]; then baudrate=57600 fi screen_startfi Juniper EX4200 booting output U-Boot 1.1.6 (May 19 2010 - 05:03:13)Board: EX4200-24T 3.12EPLD: Version 6.0 (0x85)DRAM: Initializing (1024 MB)FLASH: 8 MBUSB: scanning bus for devices... 2 USB Device(s) found scanning bus for storage devices... 1 Storage Device(s) foundELF file is 32 bitConsoles: U-Boot consoleFreeBSD/PowerPC U-Boot bootstrap loader, Revision 2.2(builder@shoth.juniper.net, Wed May 19 06:04:27 UTC 2010)Memory: 1024MBLoading /boot/defaults/loader.conf/kernel data=0x8d8e8c+0x947cc syms=[0x4+0x7a1a0+0x4+0xad2a2]Hit [Enter] to boot immediately, or space bar for command prompt.Booting [/kernel]...Kernel entry at 0x800000e0 ...GDB: no debug ports presentKDB: debugger backends: ddbKDB: current backend: ddbCopyright (c) 1996-2010, Juniper Networks, Inc.All rights reserved.Copyright (c) 1992-2006 The FreeBSD Project.Copyright (c) 1979, 1980, 1983, 1986, 1988, 1989, 1991, 1992, 1993, 1994 The Regents of the University of California. entry.title: How to use CMVC handling defects
entry.content: CMVC, stands for Configuration Management Version Control, it is an IBM internal product. GPFS uses CMVC to track defects, this article is to provide steps how to setup and use it.Request a new CMVC IDThere are many CMVC families, as a FVT/PTF member, we only need to access two families, hpssl and aix.Firstly, go to Reqauth4Me tool to request a new CMVC ID. You will be asked to input information before clicking the Submit button. Login: (Login limited to 15 alphanumeric characters)Family: (hpssl or aix)Justification: (Justification limited to 130 characters)Have better to choose a US approver to approve your request, some approver have no idea about your request. Each request only can choose one family, so you need to submit two times due to two families here.Set password for the new CMVC IDAfter the requests are approved by an approver, you will receive a system email, then you should set password on it before using it.Go to Reqauth4Me tool again, click “Query Logins” in the left menu panel, provide below information then click Submit button. Serial: (Your serial number)CMVC Login ID: (The login name you defined)Family: (hpssl or aix)A matched login will be returned in the query results, select it then click “Set Password” button to apply a password for your login ID.Obtain a CMVC ClientYou can download a CMVC client by platform from CMVC support, then install it by following up the Installation Instructions.Configuration for handling GPFS defectsWhen open a defect for GPFS, choose aix family. When open a defect for fixing hardware/software issue of the testing environment, choose hpssl family. Launch CMVC client on MacOS # java -jar CMVC.jar Click the menu File -> Startup Wizard -> Next -> Enter your CMVC login ID, then Next -> Enter the family you want to access, then Next -> Next -> Enter the component name you want to access, then Next -> Type “na” for Release -> Finish hpssl@bldcmvc01.pok.ibm.com@9999 component: gpfs.hw (for FVT) PPSLAB_software (for PTF)aix@auscmvc1.austin.ibm.com@2035 component: mmfs The process to handle defects by CMVC clientOpen a defect For GPFS defect, ensure aix family and component mmfs on CMVC client. Actions -> Defects -> Open… -> Fill below mandatory fields at least -> OK Remarks:Severity:Phase found: // post_ga for PTFcustProbabilty: For testing environment defect, ensure hpssl family and component gpfs.hw or PPSLAB_software on CMVC client. Actions -> Defects -> Open… -> Fill below mandatory fields at least -> OK Example: Remarks: Failed to upgrade the node to RHEL 8.xAbstract: c550f5u01 - Reimage RHEL 8.3Prefix: sr Severity: 2Symptom: support_requestPhase found: n/a Update a defect For GPFS defect, can update it on RTC. For testing environment defect, follow below actions to add a comment without changing other fields: Actions -> Defects -> Remarks -> Add… Re-open a defect For testing environment defect, can re-open it if its state was returned but need further assist. Actions -> Defects -> Reopen… Close a defect For GPFS defect, we can update and close it on RTC. For testing environment defect, when its state is “verify”, follow below actions to close it on CMVC client. Objects -> Defects -> Verification Records… -> Enter your CMVC login ID in the field “Owner ID”, and select “ready” in the field “State” -> OK It will show the matched defect in a new window, then right click the defect and choose “Accept…”, later the defect’s state will turn to “closed” automatically. ReferencesGPFS Defects pageCMVC information from GpfsWikiCMVC 5.0 InfoCenter document from CMVC SupportCMVC Support Home

entry.title: SLT stands setup
entry.content: SLT stands located on Tucson lab, each node can access external network. Before next actions, you should configure passwordless on all nodes in the same cluster.Kubernetes environment setupDocker-ce version: v18.09.9 - Latest validated version for K8s v1.16.xKubernetes version: v1.16.8 Firewalld disable Swapoff SELinux disable sysctl params: net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1 net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-ip6tables = 1./k8s_env_setup.sh All nodes need to run this scriptGPFS network setupOptimize the performance of GPFS communications I/OEnable Jumbo Frames with MTU 9000 and tune the TCP window settings # ping -s 8972 -M do -c 5 <external_interface_ip> The unsupported Jumbo Frames output: ping: local error: Message too long, mtu=1500Reference:Linux tuning for GPFS./gpfs_net_setup.sh 172.71.70 All nodes need to run this script, then restart GPFS.Kubernetes master init Edit /etc/hosts to add apiserver name resolution Init master node: # kubeadm init --config kubeadm-config.yaml --upload-certs Deploy a pod network to the cluster: # kubectl apply -f kube-flannel.yml HA master setup:Keepalived + haproxy as a Load BalancerLVS settings after master init: # echo "-A -t 9.11.230.x:8443 -s rr-a -t 9.11.230.x:8443 -r 9.11.230.y:6443 -m-a -t 9.11.230.x:8443 -r 9.11.230.z:6443 -m" | ipvsadm -R Kubernetes worker nodes join and create Dashboard Join worker node: # kubeadm join stand8.apiserver.tuc:8443 --token xxx \--discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:xxxx Create Dashboard: # kubectl create -f kubernetes-dashboard.yaml# kubectl create serviceaccount dashboard-admin -n kubernetes-dashboard# kubectl create clusterrolebinding dashboard-admin --clusterrole=cluster-admin --serviceaccount=kubernetes-dashboard:dashboard-admin Get Dashboard admin token: # kubectl describe secrets -n kubernetes-dashboard $(kubectl -n kubernetes-dashboard get secret | awk '/dashboard-admin/{print $1}') Install MC and Prometheus Docker login TAAS registry, update to kubelet config and restart it. Install.sh v11 for MC version 0.1.2.1_200403 # ./install.sh -p taas -y -k $api_key -v 0.1.2.1_200403 -c Edit machinecity_cr.yaml then apply it sysResource: cpuUsage: 25 # It indicates the percentage of system resource Machine City will consume, need assign 10 cores to mc-blkserver. memUsage: 50 # kubectl apply -f machinecity_cr.yaml Apply exporter-monitor.yaml: # kubectl apply -f exporter-monitor.yaml Install helm: # curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/master/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash Add helm repo: # helm repo add stable https://kubernetes-charts.storage.googleapis.com/# helm repo update Install Prometheus: # helm install my-release stable/prometheus-operator --namespace=kube-system Edit Grafana and Prometheus services to update port type: # kubectl edit svc my-release-grafana -n kube-system # kubectl edit svc my-release-prometheus-oper-prometheus -n kube-system (Optional)Install GPFS Perfmon for PrometheusMaster node run as collector/sensor, worker nodes run as sensor.Reference: Using IBM Spectrum Scale performance monitoring bridge with Grafana
